Implement the following plan:

# SFCC-89 — PDP static product information, built fresh

**Planned 2026-08-23.** Nothing built yet; no branch cut.

---

## Context

SFCC-89 ("PDP UI — static product information") already has an attempt on PR #57, by Jhoan. Its
component layer is good — `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is the best worked example of the house styling
pattern in the repo. Its integration layer is not: the page override takes over
`/product/:productId` and renders only a static panel, so **merging it removes add-to-bag, swatches,
the quantity picker, recommendations, accordions, SEO tags and 404 handling from the live PDP.**

That traces to one skipped step — the copy-first rule — which is also why its breadcrumb silently
restyled the PLP. Rebuilding correctly is cleaner than unpicking it.

Outcome wanted: SFCC-89's acceptance criteria delivered on top of an **untouched out-of-the-box
PDP**, with the genuinely shared pieces extracted as atoms that SFCC-91/92/194 can import.

---

## Decisions locked

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | Branch **`feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`**, cut from `develop` now, rebased when **PR #59** lands. |
| 2 | Clean build. #57 and SFCC-91 are read as reference so we don't build blindly — never copied from. |
| 3 | **Copy-first the PDP page.** Non-negotiable; its absence caused every integration defect in #57. |
| 4 | **`product-view` gets one override with a single optional `renderHeader` prop**, defaulting to the existing private header, so cart/wishlist/bonus-product are byte-identical unless they opt in. No speculative slots for SFCC-91/92. |
| 5 | Treat `overrides/app/components/product-view/` as **Tier 2**; notify Squad B before the PR. If sign-off outruns the sprint, proceed on the verified-approver path. |
| 6 | Model line reads **`c_modelFit`** and renders nothing when absent. No `c_sizeFit` scraping. |
| 7 | **Sanitiser: reproduce or refute the SSR crash first — hard gate.** No component code until it resolves. |
| 8 | **The page composes.** No container component mirroring `pdp/product-content`; the ported page places the pieces. |
| 9 | Page layout values as **Chakra props on the page**, not a recipe — `overrideStyling.md`'s recipe tier is scoped to variant/state on non-Chakra props, and a grid has no states. |
| 10 | Unresolved values get a **named const + comment** stating the measured value, the missing token and the owner. |
| 11 | **Recipes only where a variant or state exists.** |
| 12 | Test shape follows **PR #59**, plus the six gap closures below. |
| 13 | PR #57 stays open, closes as superseded once ours delivers. |
| 14 | `testing.md`'s `:42` wording fix deferred until after this ships. |
| 15 | The atom/molecule/organism taxonomy stays **informal** — it exists only in directory names and #59's practice, not in any repo rule. No rules PR. |

---

## Scope

**In:** product name · price · description · style code · model line · the page port.

**Out, with owners:**

| Item | Owner |
|---|---|
| **Breadcrumb** | **SFCC-578** (Squad B) — no design exists anywhere; see findings |
| Disclaimer band | **SFCC-749** / **SFCC-748** (Isabel, Squad A, epic SFCC-3) |
| Colour swatches | SFCC-91 |
| Size selector, add-to-bag | SFCC-92 |
| Image gallery | SFCC-186/187/188 |
| Accordions | SFCC-195/102/267/266 |
| Badges | SFCC-132/225 · Was/now pricing | SFCC-194 · Wishlist | SFCC-434 |
| Find in Boutique | SFCC-297 |

---

## What we build

Structured by tier, per the team's approach: atoms compose into molecules, styling lives in theme
recipes, and we override rather than rebuild so we inherit existing wiring.

**Atoms** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/<camelCase>/`, each `index.tsx` +
`index.stories.tsx`:

| Atom | Spec | Recipe? |
|---|---|---|
| `zimmProductName` | `textStyle="heading3"` | No — tiers 1–2 cover it |
| `zimmProductPrice` | `textStyle="price"` | **Yes** — `default` now; `sale` is the extension point SFCC-194 needs (`pdp/price` has both states) |
| `zimmProductDescription` | sanitised HTML, `textStyle="body2"` | **Yes** — responsive mobile inset |
| `zimmProductModelInfo` | `textStyle="caption"` | No — tiers 1–2 cover it |
| `zimmProductStyleCode` | label + value, `textStyle="caption"` | **Yes** — multipart; the DS models it as two nodes (label 57px at x=0, value 157px at x=61) |

**Molecule** — `zimmProductContent`: name + price + description. Not an invented grouping — it is
the DS's own `Content` frame (218×82). Its recipe carries the 20px internal rhythm and the
conditional margins that collapse when an optional field is absent.

**Model info and style code sit outside the molecule**, placed by the page, because the design puts
them at the bottom after the accordions rather than with the description.

**Organism** — none. `pdp/hero` is the organism and it is SFCC-723's.

**Four recipes, not six.** `overrideStyling.md`'s hierarchy puts the recipe at **tier 3** for values
needing variant, state or responsive behaviour; an atom whose whole spec is a `textStyle` plus a
token is satisfied at tiers 1–2. Same reason #59 gave `zimmTextInput` and `zimmNavItem` recipes but
not `zimmIcon` and `zimmLogo`.

**Overrides — what each inherits by overriding rather than rebuilding:**

| Override | Inherits |
|---|---|
| `pages/product-detail/` (copy-first port) | `useProduct` with its nine-field `expand` list and `perPricebook: true` · `<Helmet>`/Seo · `HTTPNotFound` 404 · `Cache-Control: s-maxage=900` · Einstein / Data Cloud / Active Data beacons |
| `components/product-view/` (one optional `renderHeader`) | add-to-cart wiring · swatch state · quantity state · the whole options column. Cart, wishlist and bonus-product stay byte-identical |

**Reuse rather than rebuild:** `utils/safeHref.ts` and the recipe patterns from #59 ·
`recipeGuards.test.ts` (auto-enforces the `Zimm` prefix) · `iconSizes` and foundation tokens as
constants · base `Skeleton`/`Box`/`Text` from `shared/ui` · base `app/components/seo`
(`react-helmet@6.1.0` already installed — no new package) · `proxyImageUrl` for image URLs ·
`intl.formatNumber` for currency.

**Styling approach:** recipe as the canonical surface for the four that need one, `Zimm`-prefixed and
registered in `theme/components/index.ts` · `textStyle` for all type, never a raw `fontSize` ·
semantic tokens for colour and space · `var(--zimm-scale-*)` where no named token exists and on
**sizing** props regardless, since `theme.sizes` is unregistered · named const + owner comment for
genuinely unsourced values · no raw literals in component files.

**Page layout values.** From `pdp/hero` Desktop Default (1440): gallery `list` x=0 w=**902**,
`pdp/product-content` x=**1082** w=**218** ⇒ gap **180**, right margin **140**.

| Value | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Column gap 180px | `var(--zimm-scale-4500)` — exact match, **not** a token gap |
| Desktop right pad 140px | `var(--zimm-scale-3500)` — exact match |
| Info column 218px | named const — no numeric alias for 218 |
| Mobile gutter 30px | import `grid.containerPadding.base` (exactly 30px; `grid` isn't a registered scale). **Not** the 32px `2xl` token. Confirmed by the mobile design: 342px column at x=30 in a 402 frame |
| Top padding 16px | bare key `m` |
| Gallery aspect ratio | plain ratio literal |

Note in the PR that **SFCC-723 (`pdp/hero`) should absorb these** into the hero organism.

---

## Test coverage requirements

#59's pattern is the basis and it is sound: move logic out into hooks, utils and exported recipe
resolvers, unit-test it there, let Storybook `play` drive the component. `AGENTS.md:151`,
`code-quality/SKILL.md:95` and `new-component/SKILL.md:50` all permit `.test.ts` **or** `play`, and
Storybook interaction + a11y are **required checks** on `develop`, so a play-only component is
genuinely gated. Its gates ran and passed on `a207b9a`, the last commit touching `overrides/`.

**Close these six gaps that #59 leaves:**

| # | Gap | What we do |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Nothing ties external data shape to props. A mis-keyed field falls to `?? ''` and renders empty — invisible to `play` and to axe. `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping first. | A co-located test for the product→props mapping: every field, including absent, asserting the right field reached the right prop. |
| G2 | Nothing asserts a recipe's declared `parts` match what the component *reads*. Drift ⇒ `__css={undefined}` ⇒ silently unstyled. | Assert `parts` ⊇ the part names the component consumes. Comparing `parts` to `baseStyle` keys is insufficient — renaming both stays green. |
| G3 | Props crossing composition boundaries are unchecked. | Assert any prop crossing more than one boundary reaches the leaf. |
| G4 | Vacuity — suites asserting "no offenders" pass on empty input. Only `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards this. | Any such suite of ours carries a self-test proving it collected something. Copy `recipeGuards.test.ts:168-174`. |
| G5 | #59 asserts focus-trap behaviour in both a hook test and a `play`, against `testing.md:3`. | One layer per behaviour; note the choice. |
| G6 | A skipped required check satisfies branch protection. Correct when only docs/tooling changed; a hole when source changed. | Before requesting review, verify the gates ran on **the last commit that touched testable source**, not merely on head. |

Concretely: the **sanitiser util** and all four **recipes** get real Vitest files (resolver branches
where they exist, plus the G2 `parts` assertion) · the five **atoms** get stories, with a `play` only
where there's real behaviour or an a11y contract — no tautological `getByRole(); toBeInTheDocument()`
· the **molecule** gets a `play` covering the absent-optional-field cases · the **page's data
mapping** gets the G1 co-located test.

---

## Build sequence

### Phase 0 — the gate. No component code until this resolves.

**Reproduce or refute the SSR crash.** Serve `build/` and request a valid and an invalid SKU;
capture the server log.

Established: the `isomorphic-dompurify` **Node entry is compiled into `build/server-renderer.js`**
(its Proxy with `get`/`apply` traps is identifiable in the minified output) and `jsdom` is a
**production** dependency pulled in by that package. **Unverified: that it actually throws.** The
original trace names `main-server.js`, a **dev-server** artifact that doesn't exist in a production
build. jsdom is a Node library and webpack's node target keeps its requires intact, so it may work
fine — in which case the TDZ error has another cause.

- **If it throws:** the engine choice is forced, and Hard Rule #7 becomes a defect report to
  Integration rather than a permission request.
- **If it doesn't:** `isomorphic-dompurify` stands as SFCC-195 documents it, and the only open
  question is 10 MB of jsdom on the SSR path — a cold-start cost, not a correctness one.

**In parallel (non-code, ungated):** cut the branch · notify Squad B about the `product-view`
override · send the designer batch · raise the findings below with Jas.

### Phase 1 — copy-first, then stop

Copy base `pages/product-detail/index.jsx` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`,
convert to TypeScript, add the temporary marker log, and verify the **full** PDP still works:
add-to-bag, swatches, quantity, gallery, accordions, recommendations, SEO tags in the served HTML,
bad SKU → 404. **Pause for testing before any functional change.** Same for `product-view` when the
header slot lands.

Everything after this is additive, so capability cannot be lost.

### Phase 2 — sanitiser util, then atoms bottom-up

1. `utils/sanitiseHtml.ts` + `sanitiseHtml.test.ts` — every rejection case as a row. Engine decided
   by Phase 0's outcome; the util is the seam either way, so a later engine swap is one file.
2. The five atoms, each with a story. Recipes for `zimmProductPrice`, `zimmProductDescription` and
   `zimmProductStyleCode` in `theme/components/`, registered in that folder's `index.ts`. Names must
   be `Zimm`-prefixed — base SFCC registers its own recipes and `extendTheme` deep-merges on a key
   collision. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this automatically once #59 lands.

### Phase 3 — the molecule

`zimmProductContent` composing name + price + description, with its recipe holding the 20px internal
rhythm and the conditional margins. A `play` covering the absent-optional-field cases.

### Phase 4 — integrate

Place the molecule, then model info and style code at their own positions further down, in the
ported page. Remove the copy-first markers. **Name every base behaviour deliberately changed in the
PR body.**

---

## Verification

**Mechanical** — none is CI-gated, so all are honour-system and must actually be run:
`npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run lint` (17 pre-existing Contentful errors; ours must add none) ·
`npx vitest run` · `npm run build` then `npm run test:max-file-size` (**vendor sits at 95.4% of
budget** — read the headroom, not the pass) · `npx test-storybook --ci` against a built Storybook.

**Parity — the check that matters.** Re-run Phase 1's checklist against the finished page: add-to-bag
completes · a swatch changes the variant · quantity works · the gallery renders **through
`proxyImageUrl`** (direct Demandware access is Cloudflare-WAF-blocked outside the CC network, so
without it real shoppers get a 403) · accordions open · all three recommendation rails render · SEO
tags present in the **served** HTML · unknown SKU returns **404**, not 200.

**Acceptance criteria**, against live SFCC data: name · single full price in storefront currency ·
description · style code (**master style number, not `product.id`**) · model copy present when
`c_modelFit` exists and cleanly absent when it doesn't.

**Before requesting review** — per G6, confirm the gates ran on the last commit touching testable
source.

---

## Critical files

**Create:**
`ui-kits/atoms/{zimmProductName,zimmProductPrice,zimmProductDescription,zimmProductModelInfo,zimmProductStyleCode}/`
· `ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/` ·
`theme/components/{zimmProductPrice,zimmProductDescription,zimmProductStyleCode,zimmProductContent}.ts`
· `utils/sanitiseHtml.ts` + test · `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (copy-first port) + its
data-mapping test · `components/product-view/` (scoped override)

**Modify:** `theme/components/index.ts` (registration) · `types/` for any new `c_*` narrowing.
`routes.tsx` **only if** the port needs it — the base route already resolves to the base page, so an
explicit entry is probably unnecessary.

**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `utils/safeHref.ts` (#59) · `utils/sfccImage.ts`'s `proxyImageUrl()` ·
`iconSizes` from `theme/foundation` · base `Skeleton`/`Box`/`Text` · base
`app/components/seo` — **`react-helmet@6.1.0` is already installed** as a `retail-react-app`
dependency, so SEO needs no new package.

---

## Verified corrections — do not relitigate

- **One shadowing mechanism, not two.** The resolver only redirects imports *naming* a package in
  `extends`; base `routes.jsx:43` uses a relative `import('./pages/product-detail')`, so it is never
  redirected. Removing `overrides/app/routes.tsx:37-40` alone restores the base PDP.
- **`Skeleton height="var(--zimm-scale-*)"` is correct.** `theme/index.ts` registers `space` but not
  `sizes`, so a bare key on a sizing prop misresolves.
- **`frozenFiles.md` is correct about fonts on `develop`** — none, by licence. #59 brings
  self-hosting, which is the agreed approach. Until it merges, no type metric is visually verifiable.
- **Base `categoryUrlBuilder` ignores the locale argument** it's handed. No multi-site routing bug.
- **`@storybook/test` doesn't exist** on Storybook 10 — import from `storybook/test`.
  `.claude/rules/testing.md:87` is wrong.
- **PR #55 is closed; #59 is live** on the same branch. #55 had no fonts and 8 recipes; #59 has both
  fonts and 10.
- **`<Island>` is inert** — `config/default.js:40` sets `partialHydrationEnabled: false`.
- **The composition order differs from #57**: name → price → description → colour → size → CTAs →
  accordions → **model line → style code**. Model copy and style code sit at the **bottom**.

---

## Design-system findings

- `pdp/hero` and `pdp/product-content` are real DS components, four variants each. 218px info column
  confirmed three ways.
- Vertical rhythm: **20px** within the text group (= `spacing.l`), **28px** between blocks, **44px**
  after the content group.
- Product name is capped at **180px** in a 218px row, wishlist at x=194–218.
- **Only `Price` is a Figma component** in scope. Name, description, model copy and style code are
  `text` nodes inside `frame` containers.
- Desktop page gutter is **40px**, consistent across four components.
- **DS-versus-page inconsistencies** (both real, for the designer):
  - `Button Large` is **52** in the DS component, **50** in both composed pages.
  - `styleCode` is **two nodes** (label + value) in the DS, **one** in both composed pages
    (`"Style Code: 7300JS261"`). #57's concatenation matches the pages.

---

## Findings to raise

**1. AC-6 asks for a breadcrumb that was never designed.** Checked: the design system by name, both
PDP components, both PLP bars at both breakpoints, both non-archived PDP designs in full, and the
Footer. The only appearance is placeholder copy in the **Disclaimer's Contentful-driven title field**
(SFCC-749 gives its example as *"TERMS AND CONDITIONS"*) — and a breadcrumb is derived at runtime
from the category path, so it structurally cannot be that field. #57's `/` separator and uppercase
were copied from that placeholder, not from a spec. → **Jas**, with SFCC-578 as the owner.

**2. Duplicate scope, three instances, all created 17 Aug and all "In Refinement":**

| Built / building | Duplicate |
|---|---|
| SFCC-89 | SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content` |
| SFCC-89's breadcrumb | SFCC-578 SEO Breadcrumb (Squad B) |
| SFCC-55 / PR #59 footer | SFCC-750 Footer – PWA Kit Component |

Systemic decomposition drift, not three coincidences. Raise as a pattern. SFCC-749's description
also self-links instead of pointing at SFCC-748, suggesting a batch created without a review pass.

**3. No page server-renders on the PR-57 preview or the `test` tier** — every route returns HTTP 200
with a `loadable` fallback spinner. Pre-existing, storefront-wide, and it defeats the ≤2s p75 LCP
budget. Likely `ChunkExtractor`/`loadable-stats.json` wiring in `ssr.js` — **Tier 1, Integration
only, do not attempt.** Also means MRT preview is not a usable SSR smoke test. Unknown whether
`staging`/`prod` behave the same.

**4. Ownership contradiction on `pages/product-detail/`:** `CODEOWNERS:159` says Squad B;
`.claude/rules/squadA.md:4,34` says Squad A; `.claude/registry/pages.md:20` says Squad A / Tier 4.
Recorded 2026-07-09 and still open. CODEOWNERS is the enforced surface. **Output must be a commit to
one governance file.**

**5. Repo rules that are wrong or missing:** `testing.md:87`'s broken `@storybook/test` import ·
`overrideStyling.md` mandates `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`, which doesn't exist ·
`.claude/rules/overrides.md` is cross-referenced but absent from `develop` (it exists on
`f2r-component-registry` and contains the override pre-flight that would have caught #57's defects)
· no i18n rule exists anywhere, on a project with 11 locales.

## Designer batch

Which node is canonical (five in circulation) · **Button 50 vs 52** (DS vs composed pages) ·
**style code one node or two** (DS vs composed pages) · the **28px** and **44px** gaps — keep or
tokenise · `FONT_REGULAR` vs `FONT_MEDIUM` for price and meta copy (#57's recipe flags this
correctly) · the **768–1279px band is undesigned** (DS has 402 and 1440 only) · `body2Strong`
letter-spacing points at −0.12px where Figma reads −0.14px and `letterSpacings['2xs']` already holds
−0.14px (Tier 1, no PDP consumer — batch it) · `#000000` vs `text.default` on two labels.


If you need specific details from before exiting plan mode (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/projects/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/723a905e-37fe-4505-9a24-e817fe4260ab.jsonl

## Test coverage requirements

#59's pattern is the basis and it is sound: move logic out into hooks, utils and exported recipe
resolvers, unit-test it there, let Storybook `play` drive the component. `AGENTS.md:151`,
`code-quality/SKILL.md:95` and `new-component/SKILL.md:50` all permit `.test.ts` **or** `play`, and
Storybook interaction + a11y are **required checks** on `develop`, so a play-only component is
genuinely gated. Its gates ran and passed on `a207b9a`, the last commit touching `overrides/`.

**Close these six gaps that #59 leaves:**

| # | Gap | What we do |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | Nothing ties external data shape to props. A mis-keyed field falls to `?? ''` and renders empty — invisible to `play` and to axe. `testing.md:19` ranks data mapping first. | A co-located test for the product→props mapping: every field, including absent, asserting the right field reached the right prop. |
| G2 | Nothing asserts a recipe's declared `parts` match what the component *reads*. Drift ⇒ `__css={undefined}` ⇒ silently unstyled. | Assert `parts` ⊇ the part names the component consumes. Comparing `parts` to `baseStyle` keys is insufficient — renaming both stays green. |
| G3 | Props crossing composition boundaries are unchecked. | Assert any prop crossing more than one boundary reaches the leaf. |
| G4 | Vacuity — suites asserting "no offenders" pass on empty input. Only `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards this. | Any such suite of ours carries a self-test proving it collected something. Copy `recipeGuards.test.ts:168-174`. |
| G5 | #59 asserts focus-trap behaviour in both a hook test and a `play`, against `testing.md:3`. | One layer per behaviour; note the choice. |
| G6 | A skipped required check satisfies branch protection. Correct when only docs/tooling changed; a hole when source changed. | Before requesting review, verify the gates ran on **the last commit that touched testable source**, not merely on head. |

Concretely: the **sanitiser util** and all four **recipes** get real Vitest files (resolver branches
where they exist, plus the G2 `parts` assertion) · the five **atoms** get stories, with a `play` only
where there's real behaviour or an a11y contract — no tautological `getByRole(); toBeInTheDocument()`
· the **molecule** gets a `play` covering the absent-optional-field cases · the **page's data
mapping** gets the G1 co-located test.

### Phase 0 — the gate. No component code until this resolves.

**Reproduce or refute the SSR crash.** Serve `build/` and request a valid and an invalid SKU;
capture the server log.

Established: the `isomorphic-dompurify` **Node entry is compiled into `build/server-renderer.js`**
(its Proxy with `get`/`apply` traps is identifiable in the minified output) and `jsdom` is a
**production** dependency pulled in by that package. **Unverified: that it actually throws.** The
original trace names `main-server.js`, a **dev-server** artifact that doesn't exist in a production
build. jsdom is a Node library and webpack's node target keeps its requires intact, so it may work
fine — in which case the TDZ error has another cause.

- **If it throws:** the engine choice is forced, and Hard Rule #7 becomes a defect report to
  Integration rather than a permission request.
- **If it doesn't:** `isomorphic-dompurify` stands as SFCC-195 documents it, and the only open
  question is 10 MB of jsdom on the SSR path — a cold-start cost, not a correctness one.

**In parallel (non-code, ungated):** cut the branch · notify Squad B about the `product-view`
override · send the designer batch · raise the findings below with Jas.

### Phase 1 — copy-first, then stop

Copy base `pages/product-detail/index.jsx` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`,
convert to TypeScript, add the temporary marker log, and verify the **full** PDP still works:
add-to-bag, swatches, quantity, gallery, accordions, recommendations, SEO tags in the served HTML,
bad SKU → 404. **Pause for testing before any functional change.** Same for `product-view` when the
header slot lands.

Everything after this is additive, so capability cannot be lost.

### Phase 2 — sanitiser util, then atoms bottom-up

1. `utils/sanitiseHtml.ts` + `sanitiseHtml.test.ts` — every rejection case as a row. Engine decided
   by Phase 0's outcome; the util is the seam either way, so a later engine swap is one file.
2. The five atoms, each with a story. Recipes for `zimmProductPrice`, `zimmProductDescription` and
   `zimmProductStyleCode` in `theme/components/`, registered in that folder's `index.ts`. Names must
   be `Zimm`-prefixed — base SFCC registers its own recipes and `extendTheme` deep-merges on a key
   collision. `recipeGuards.test.ts` enforces this automatically once #59 lands.

### Phase 3 — the molecule

`zimmProductContent` composing name + price + description, with its recipe holding the 20px internal
rhythm and the conditional margins. A `play` covering the absent-optional-field cases.

### Phase 4 — integrate

In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. <function call omitted for brevity>

This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>

The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. ## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md

- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.
- vercel:deploy: Deploy the current project to Vercel. Pass "prod" or "production" as argument to deploy to production. Default is preview deployment.
- vercel:env: Manage Vercel environment variables. Commands include list, pull, add, remove, and diff. Use to sync environment variables between Vercel and your local development environment.
- vercel:status: Show the status of the current Vercel project — recent deployments, linked project info, and environment overview.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- superpowers:brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
- superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
- superpowers:executing-plans: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints
- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

- plugin-dev:hook-development: This skill should be used when the user asks to "create a hook", "add a PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hook", "validate tool use", "implement prompt-based hooks", "use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}", "set up event-driven automation", "block dangerous commands", or mentions hook events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, Notification). Provides comprehensive guidance for integrating Model Context Protocol servers into Claude Code plugins for external tool and service integration.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. /*
 * The PDP override is reached through this explicit entry, not through the overrides
 * resolver. That resolver only redirects imports that *name* `@salesforce/retail-react-app`;
 * the base `app/routes.jsx` loads its PDP with a relative `import('./pages/product-detail')`,

 * is dead code and the base page renders instead.
 */
const ProductDetail = loadable(() => import('./pages/product-detail'), { fallback });"""
assert old_imports in s
s = s.replace(old_imports, new_imports, 1)

    path: '/my-new-route',

  {
    path: '/product/:productId',
    component: ProductDetail,
  },
  ..._routes,"""
assert old_route in s

* Render a product detail view that includes name, image gallery, price,
 * variant selections, action buttons
 */

const ProductView = forwardRef(
  (
    {
      product,
      category,
      showFullLink = false,
      imageSize = 'md',
      isWishlistLoading = false,
      addToCart,
      updateCart,
      addToWishlist,
      updateWishlist,
      isProductLoading,
      isProductPartOfSet = false,
      isProductPartOfBundle = false,
      childOfBundleQuantity = 0,
      childProductOrderability,
      setChildProductOrderability,
      isBasketLoading = false,
      onVariantSelected = () => {},
      validateOrderability = (variant, product, quantity, stockLevel) => {
        if (isProductLoading) return false;

        // If product has variations, a variant must be selected
        if (product?.variationAttributes?.length > 0 && !variant) {
          return false;
        }

        // Check if product (either variant or standard) is orderable and if quantity is valid
        return (variant?.orderable || product?.inventory?.orderable) && quantity > 0 && quantity <= stockLevel;
      },
      showImageGallery = true,
      setSelectedBundleQuantity = () => {},
      selectedBundleParentQuantity = 1,
      pickupInStore = false,
      setPickupInStore = () => {},
      onOpenStoreLocator = () => {},
      showDeliveryOptions = true,
      customButtons = [],
      maxOrderQuantity = null,
      imageGalleryFooter = null,
      controlledVariationValues = null,
      onVariationChange = null,
    },
    ref,
  ) => {
    const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
    const showToast = useToast();
    const intl = useIntl();
    const location = useLocation();
    const storeLocatorEnabled = getConfig()?.app?.storeLocatorEnabled ?? STORE_LOCATOR_IS_ENABLED;
    const {
      isOpen: isAddToCartModalOpen,
      onOpen: onAddToCartModalOpen,
      onClose: onAddToCartModalClose,
    } = useAddToCartModalContext();

    const { mutateAsync: createBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutation('createBasket');
    const { mutateAsync: addItemToBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutation('addItemToBasket');

    const theme = useTheme();
    const { confirmingBasket } = useSFPayments();
    const [showOptionsMessage, toggleShowOptionsMessage] = useState(false);
    const {
      showLoading,
      showInventoryMessage,
      inventoryMessage,
      quantity,
      minOrderQuantity,
      setQuantity,
      variant,
      variationParams,

content.subject: Phase 0 — reproduce or refute the SSR sanitiser crash
content.description: Hard gate. Serve build/ and request a valid + invalid SKU; capture server log. Determine whether isomorphic-dompurify's Node entry actually throws under SSR in a production build. Outcome decides the sanitiser engine.

content.subject: Cut feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info from develop
content.description: Clean branch from develop, per decision 1. Current branch is the old #57-era attempt and must not be built on.

content.subject: Phase 1 — copy-first port of pages/product-detail
content.description: Copy base pages/product-detail/index.jsx to overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx, convert to TS, add temporary marker log, verify full PDP parity. Pause for user testing before any functional change.

content.subject: Phase 2 — sanitiser util + five atoms
content.description: utils/sanitiseHtml.ts + test (every rejection case as a row). Then zimmProductName, zimmProductPrice, zimmProductDescription, zimmProductModelInfo, zimmProductStyleCode with stories; recipes for price/description/styleCode registered in theme/components/index.ts.

content.subject: Phase 3 — zimmProductContent molecule
content.description: Molecule composing name + price + description, recipe holding the 20px internal rhythm and conditional margins. play covering absent-optional-field cases.

content.subject: Phase 4 — integrate into the ported page
content.description: Place molecule, then model info + style code lower down. product-view renderHeader override. Remove copy-first markers. G1 data-mapping test.

content.subject: Verification — mechanical + parity + acceptance criteria
content.description: tsc, lint, vitest, build + max-file-size, test-storybook. Then Phase 1 parity checklist re-run against finished page. Then AC checks against live SFCC data. G6 gate check before review.

new = """/*
 * Relative, not `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view`. The overrides
 * resolver (pwa-kit-dev's OverridesResolverPlugin) deliberately skips any request whose
 * issuer already lives in `overrides/` — see its `isFromExtends` guard — so a base-path
 * import from this file resolves to the *base* component even in the real app build, not
 * just in Storybook/Vitest. Base callers (cart, wishlist, bonus-product) still reach our
 * override, because their issuer is inside node_modules and so is redirected normally.
 */
import ProductView from '../../components/product-view';"""
assert old in s
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new,1))

PY

/**
 * Recipe guards — regression tests for four failure modes that reached a feature branch
 * despite passing `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit and the Storybook a11y run.
 *
 * All four share a shape: the value is a *valid* `SystemStyleObject` entry, so TypeScript is
 * satisfied; no lint rule covers it; and nothing asserts layout. Each one renders plausible,
 * wrong output that is only visible by opening the page.
 *
 *   1. A spacing-scale key on a sizing property. Chakra resolves `width`/`height`/`boxSize`
 *      through `theme.sizes`, not `theme.space`. The Zimmermann named scale is registered as
 *      `space` only (deliberately — see foundation/sizes.ts), so `width: 'xl'` silently reads
 *      Chakra's default `sizes.xl` = 36rem. It shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer.
 *
 *   2. The same trap on a typography property. `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are
 *      deliberately NOT registered either (theme/index.ts explains why), so a bare key reads
 *      Chakra's default or resolves to nothing at all. See TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS below.
 *
 *   3. A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe. `theme/index.ts` composes with
 *      `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which DEEP MERGES — a recipe named `Footer` does
 *      not replace SFCC's `Footer`, it inherits it. Shared part names then pick up base
 *      properties, and a key you add that the base lacks is appended last, so a CSS shorthand
 *      can silently reset a longhand the base declared earlier.
 *
 *   4. A bare scale key inside a compound shorthand. Chakra resolves a token only when it is
 *      the entire value; `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim, the browser rejects the
 *      declaration, and the padding does not apply at all.
 *
 * A fifth guard below (`no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered
 * scale`) is a different kind of check — not a wrong-value bug, since `space` and `colors`
 * ARE registered Chakra scales (theme/index.ts), so a bare key there resolves to the correct
 * Zimmermann value either way. It enforces a house style instead: override components must
 * always reference a zimm value via `var(--zimm-scale-*)` / `var(--zimm-color-*)`, never a
 * bare Chakra token string, so a PR reviewer sees an unambiguous zimm reference at every call
 * site instead of having to recall which scales are and are not registered.
 *
 * SCOPE: these guards walk the registered recipe map only (`components` + the composed
 * `theme`). They cannot see the same mistakes made as a JSX prop on a component — there is a
 * live instance of failure mode 2 at `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302`
 * (`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing) that no test here can reach. Catching that class needs
 * a static rule over JSX attributes (`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`), not a theme walk. The
 * house-style guard has the same JSX blind spot — `footerNavColumn/index.tsx` had a bare
 * `paddingLeft: '2xs'` in an inline `sx` merge (not a recipe) that this test cannot see;
 * it was only found by a manual grep across `overrides/app/components/`, not by this suite.
 */
import { describe, expect, test } from 'vitest';
import theme from '../index';
import { components } from './index';
import { breakpoints } from '../foundation/gridSystem';
import { fontSizes, letterSpacings, lineHeights } from '../foundation/typography';
import { spacing } from '../foundation/spacing';
import { colors } from '../foundation/colour';

const SPACING_KEYS = Object.keys(spacing);

/**
 * Recursively flattens a nested token object into dot-joined path strings — 'text.default',
 * 'action.primary.bgDefault', etc. — mirroring exactly how a recipe would reference it bare
 * (`color: 'text.default'`).
 */
const flattenKeys = (obj: Record<string, unknown>, prefix = ''): string[] =>
  Object.entries(obj).flatMap(([key, value]) => {
    const path = prefix ? `${prefix}.${key}` : key;
    return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null ? flattenKeys(value as Record<string, unknown>, path) : [path];
  });

content.content:
# to storybook-static/, served by http-server, tested by test-storybook.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  storybook-test:
    name: Storybook interaction & a11y tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Build Storybook
        run: npm run build-storybook

      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
        run: |
          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
        env:
          CI: true

      - name: Upload Storybook test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: storybook-test-results
          path: storybook-test-results/
          retention-days: 30

content.text:
Done. All phases complete, verified against live SFCC data.

## Where it lives

Branch **`feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`**, cut clean from `develop` (`cd68e97`). 26 files staged, **not committed** — Hard Rule #15.

## Phase 0 — the gate: crash CONFIRMED, different cause

The TDZ hypothesis was wrong. The actual failure:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<...>/browser/default-stylesheet.css'
  at jsdom/lib/jsdom/living/css/helpers/computed-style.js:18
```

jsdom reads that asset with `fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(__dirname, '../../../browser/default-stylesheet.css'))` **at module scope**. webpack bundles jsdom into the server bundle but leaves `__dirname` as the *bundle's* directory, so the path escapes the project. It throws on **import**, before `sanitize()` is ever called — so merely importing `isomorphic-dompurify` anywhere in the SSR graph 500s the whole page. Reproduced live: PDP went 200 → 500 with a probe in place, clean when reverted. The production bundle emits the identical read and `build/` never receives the asset, so it fails the same way.

This is a plausible explanation for finding #3 (preview returning 200 with a fallback spinner). Worth handing to Integration as a defect report.

Per your choice, `utils/richText.tsx` parses to React elements — nothing reaches `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

## Two corrections to the plan

**The resolver refuses imports issued from `overrides/`.** `OverridesResolverPlugin.isFromExtends` has `!filepath.includes(issuerPath)`. So a base-path import inside an override resolves to the **base** component *in the real app build*, not just in Storybook/Vitest — `overrideStyling.md` says otherwise and is wrong. Caught it because the product-view marker never logged. The page now imports `../../components/product-view`; base callers (cart, wishlist, bonus-product) still get our override, since their issuer is in `node_modules`.

**`routes.tsx` was required, not "probably unnecessary".** Base `routes.jsx:43` uses a relative `import('./pages/product-detail')`, so the override was dead code until an explicit route entry landed.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run` | 221 passed (was 141) |
| `npm run lint` | 19 errors — **exactly** the `develop` baseline (17 Contentful + 2 pre-existing `routes.tsx` prettier). Zero added |
| `npm run test:max-file-size` | main 103.18/180 kB, vendor 515.01/550 kB (93.6%). No new deps, so vendor is unchanged by construction |
| `test-storybook --ci` | 31 passed, 11 suites |
| Parity vs base | product-view, 17 accordion nodes, swatches, add-to-cart, all 3 rails, gallery, breadcrumb, quantity — all identical; bad SKU → 404 |
| AC (live) | name ✓ · `A$895.00` (matches base's own formatting) ✓ · description ✓ · `Style Code: 8637DS241` = master style number ✓ · model line correctly absent ✓ |

Three bugs were caught by tests failing on purpose, not by inspection: `<embed>` (void element) made the drop-region swallow the rest of the document; the molecule's `& > * + *` silently lost to the child recipes' `margin: 0` (now a flex `gap`); and the recipe-parts guard was proven to fail before its pass counted.

CodeRabbit: 2 real findings fixed. Its third — "no story for ZimmProductStyleCode" — is a false positive; the file is in its own reviewed list.

## Four things needing your call

1. **`c_modelFit` does not exist on any product I checked** (3 SKUs). `c_sizeFit` does, and contains the model copy. Decision #6 forbids scraping it, so the implementation is correct and the model line will simply never render until the attribute is created and populated in Business Manager.
2. **The description now renders twice** — in the content group and in `InformationAccordion`'s "Product Detail" panel, which reads the same `longDescription`. The DS shows both; the accordion tickets (SFCC-195/102/267/266) own the resolution. Flagging rather than silently deciding.
3. **Translations reverted.** `npm run build` regenerated them and swept in two out-of-scope changes — a new `header.button.assistive_msg.search` key and `product_view.label.quantity` changing from "Quantity" to "Quantity:". Tier 2, Integration-owned. `product_detail.label.style_code` renders from its `defaultMessage`; adding it properly needs a deliberate pass by whoever owns translations.
4. **Hero layout metrics not applied.** The 180px gap, 218px column, 140px right margin and gallery ratio all live *inside* ProductView's flex, and touching it would break decision #4's byte-identical guarantee for cart/wishlist/bonus-product. Measured and documented for SFCC-723.

Also deviating deliberately: the price recipe ships `default` only — a `sale` variant echoing it would look finished and be wrong, so the extension point is documented for SFCC-194 instead.

## Next command

```bash
node build/ssr.js   # then http://localhost:3000/product/8637DS241
```

Background servers are stopped. What's left is the interactive parity pass I can't automate — add-to-bag completing, a swatch changing the variant, quantity, accordions opening.

content.content:

content.text:
Compared both branches directly. Also — the investigation caught a factual error in my own code comment; I've corrected it (details at the end).

## The core difference

His page **replaces** the PDP; ours **ports** it and adds to it.

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — his is **95 lines written from scratch**, mine is **830 lines copied from the 876-line base** and converted. His routes entry takes over `/product/:productId` exactly as mine does, so whatever his page omits is gone from the live PDP.

What his page calls: `useProduct({parameters: {id: productId}})` — no `expand`, no `perPricebook`, no `allImages`, no `inventoryIds`. What it renders: a grey `<Box>` placeholder for the gallery, `PdpProductInfo`, and a breadcrumb toolbar.

So merging #57 as-is removes from the live PDP:

| Gone | Because |
|---|---|
| Add-to-bag, swatches, quantity, delivery options | no `ProductView` at all |
| All accordions | no `InformationAccordion` |
| All three recommendation rails | no `RecommendedProducts` |
| SEO title + meta tags | no `<Helmet>` |
| **404 on a bad SKU** | no `HTTPNotFound` — renders "Unable to load product information." at HTTP **200** |
| `Cache-Control: s-maxage=900` | not set |
| Einstein / Data Cloud / Active Data beacons | not called |
| Variant→URL sync | no `useVariant` |
| The real gallery | placeholder box; `allImages` never requested |

Ours keeps all of it — I diffed the rendered HTML against the base and every marker matched (17 accordion nodes, 3 swatch nodes, 4 add-to-cart, all three rails, 6 gallery nodes, breadcrumb, quantity), with our content purely additive.

## Where the two disagree on the spec itself

These aren't quality differences, they're different readings — and the plan's locked decisions went the other way on three of them:

| | His | Ours |
|---|---|---|
| Style code | `product.id` | `product.master.masterId` — `product.id` becomes the *variant SKU* after the first swatch click |
| Model line | `extractModelLine(c_sizeFit)` — regexes the "Model is" bullet out of the size-and-fit list | reads `c_modelFit`; decision #6 forbids the scrape |
| Description | `shortDescription \|\| longDescription` | `longDescription` |
| Info column | `PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'` | DS measures 218px (confirmed three ways in the plan) |
| `var(--zimm-*)` | in component JSX (`columnGap`, `pl`, `pr`) | in theme recipes only — the styling-layer boundary |

Worth saying plainly: his `c_sizeFit` scrape is the one that *actually produces a model line today*. I checked three live products — **`c_modelFit` doesn't exist on any of them**, `c_sizeFit` does. So our decision-#6-compliant version renders nothing until that attribute is created in Business Manager. His renders the copy. That's a real trade-off, not a win for us.

## What his has that ours doesn't

- **E2E**: a 10-scenario `.feature` file and a Playwright spec with 10 tests (3 skipped pending sandbox products). We have none — the plan scoped E2E out.
- **Breadcrumb component** (86 lines) + `ZimmPageToolbar` atom. Ours defers breadcrumb to SFCC-578.
- **Registry tooling**: `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` taught to parse discriminated-union prop types.
- A Storybook story for the page assembly.

## What ours has that his doesn't

The copy-first port and the `product-view` override with one `renderHeader` slot; the rich-text parser with a 63-test rejection matrix; the G1 data-mapping test (15 tests); the G2 recipe-parts guard, proven to fail on purpose. 80 new unit tests against his 5, but his 5 cover a function we deliberately don't have.

## The dependency

His branch adds **`isomorphic-dompurify`** to `package.json` — a new production dependency, which Hard Rule #7 gates on Integration approval. That's also the package Phase 0 proved crashes SSR: importing it anywhere in the graph turns a 200 into a 500, at import time, before `sanitize()` is ever called. So that addition shouldn't be accepted as-is regardless of which branch wins.

His component layer is genuinely the better-worked one, though — `PdpProductInfo` driving everything through `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmPdpProductInfo')` with the styling in a theme config is the pattern I followed for the atoms.

## Correction to my own work

Investigating this, I found my `richText.tsx` header said `isomorphic-dompurify` is something "this repo already depends on". That's false — it's not on `develop` or our branch; **his branch adds it**. I'd read `package.json` in my first few commands while still sitting on his branch and carried the assumption forward. Comment corrected to attribute it to #57; tsc clean, 63 tests still green, lint still at the 19-error baseline. Nothing else depended on it — the Phase 0 finding itself is unaffected, and if anything it reads stronger now: it's a reason to reject a proposed dependency rather than a defect in one we already ship.

content.content:
# Testing Conventions

Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
below for single-parent internal components still applies there.

| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |

> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

---

content.text:
Two things to correct there.

## It wasn't a rebase

Our branch had **zero commits** — nothing to replay. The reflog shows what actually happened:

```
8362b3c HEAD@{0}: merge develop: Fast-forward
cd68e97 HEAD@{1}: checkout: moving from develop to feature/SFCC-89...
8362b3c HEAD@{2}: merge origin/develop: Fast-forward
```

The sequence was: **stash the 29 files → fast-forward `develop` → fast-forward the branch ref onto it → `git stash pop`**. The ref just slid forward; the work was carried across in the stash and reapplied as a 3-way merge. Functionally equivalent to a rebase, but no commits were replayed because none exist.

## There were conflicts — one git caught, one it didn't

26 of our 29 files are brand-new, so they can't conflict. Only **two** files were touched by both us and the 94 new develop commits:

**`theme/components/index.ts` — conflicted properly.** `git stash pop --index` refused outright ("patch does not apply"), then a plain pop left conflict markers. Both sides had rewritten the import block: #59 moved `Button` from `./button` to `zimmButton.css` and added eight recipes; we'd added four. I hand-merged it — 16 imports now, all twelve of theirs plus our four.

**`vendor.d.ts` — merged cleanly and was wrong.** This is the one worth knowing about. #59 had already added `useHistory` and `interface History` to the react-router shim. Our stash added its own copy in a different part of the file, so git saw two non-overlapping insertions and merged both without a murmur. TypeScript then accepted it too — interface declaration merging plus overload resolution meant `tsc` stayed at **0 errors** with a duplicated declaration sitting in a shared type file.

Only `eslint`'s `adjacent-overload-signatures` caught it. I removed ours and kept develop's, since theirs covers the one call we make (`history.replace(string)`).

So: a clean `tsc` after the merge would have told you nothing. That's why I ran lint and the full suite rather than stopping at the typecheck.

Beyond the merge itself, three further changes were needed — not conflicts, but conformance to rules that landed with #59: the `useUiCopy` microcopy switch, and three component test files the new `testing.md` requires.

content.content:
# SFCC-89 — PDP static product information, built fresh

**Planned 2026-08-23.** Nothing built yet; no branch cut.

---

## Context

SFCC-89 ("PDP UI — static product information") already has an attempt on PR #57, by Jhoan. Its
component layer is good — `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is the best worked example of the house styling
pattern in the repo. Its integration layer is not: the page override takes over
`/product/:productId` and renders only a static panel, so **merging it removes add-to-bag, swatches,
the quantity picker, recommendations, accordions, SEO tags and 404 handling from the live PDP.**

That traces to one skipped step — the copy-first rule — which is also why its breadcrumb silently
restyled the PLP. Rebuilding correctly is cleaner than unpicking it.

Outcome wanted: SFCC-89's acceptance criteria delivered on top of an **untouched out-of-the-box
PDP**, with the genuinely shared pieces extracted as atoms that SFCC-91/92/194 can import.

---

## Decisions locked

# The UI build approach established by PR #59 (merge `8362b3c`, 132 files, +8724/−1187)

## 1. Component structure — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`

#59 created the directory from scratch. At the merge commit it contains **10 components** in three tiers (all `zimm`-prefixed, camelCase folder, always `index.tsx` as the entry):

- **atoms/** — `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmModal`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput`
- **molecules/** — `zimmContactIconRow`, `zimmInputAction`
- **organisms/** — `zimmSubscribeModal`, `zimmSubscribeSection`

Composition strictly climbs the ladder: `zimmInputAction` (molecule) = `zimmTextInput` + `zimmButton`; `zimmSubscribeModal` (organism) = `zimmModal` atom + `zimmTextInput` + `zimmButton` + `useZimmModal`; `zimmSubscribeSection` (organism) = `zimmInputAction` + `zimmSubscribeModal` + `useSubscribeSection`. The footer at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` is the assembly consumer — it imports organisms rather than defining them inline.

### Representative file sets

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/`** — the fullest example (4 files):
- `index.tsx` — presentational only. Declares a local `ZimmTextInputProps` type, calls `useZimmTextInputState` for value/focus, calls `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', {inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled})`, and renders `chakra.div`/`chakra.input`/`chakra.label` with `__css={styles.<part>}`. Zero inline style values.
- `zimmTextInput.css.ts` — the Chakra multi-part recipe: `{parts: [...8 names], baseStyle: (props) => Record<string, SystemStyleObject>}`. Function-form baseStyle. Also exports three pure resolvers (`resolveBorderColour`, `resolveHoverBorderColour`, `resolveLabelColour`) and the `ZimmTextInputStyleProps` type.
- `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` — unit tests for the resolvers + recipe wiring.
- `index.stories.tsx` — `Meta`/`StoryObj` under title `Elements/ZimmTextInput`, with `argTypes` controls and 3 `play` functions.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/`** (4 files): `index.tsx`, `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts` (plain-object `baseStyle`, 5 parts), `index.test.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx` (no `play` — deliberately delegated upward, see §6).

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/`** (3 files): `index.tsx` (portal + backdrop + `role="dialog"`, `maxWidth` is a *required* prop with no default), `zimmModal.css.ts` (3 parts: overlay/panel/actions), `index.stories.tsx`. No test file — its mechanics live in `useZimmModal` and are tested there.

Atoms with no recipe file at all — `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo` — style by importing `iconSizes` from `app/theme/foundation` directly, which is the documented escape for the unregistered scales.

## 2. Styling — the co-located `.css.ts` recipe pattern

This is the single biggest structural change. Before #59, per-component styling lived in `overrides/app/theme/components/<name>.ts`. #59 **deleted `theme/components/button.ts` (−119 lines)** and moved it to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`.

**What is registered where.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` is now mostly an *import manifest pointing back out into `components/`*. 9 of its 12 entries import from a co-located `.css.ts`; only `Header`, `ListMenu` (and the `navConstants.ts` helper) still physically live in `theme/components/`. Registered keys: `Button`, `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmFooterNavColumn`, `ZimmFooterBottomBar`, `ZimmModal`, `ZimmSubscribeModal`, `ZimmSubscribeSection`, `ZimmContactIconRow`, `Header`, `ListMenu`, `ZimmNavItem`, `ZimmTextInput`.

Chakra resolves a recipe by the *string key* passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, so file location is purely organisational — every component defines a `const ZIMM_X_RECIPE = 'ZimmX'` constant at the top of `index.tsx`.

**How values are expressed.** The hierarchy in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` was rewritten by #59. Point 2 flipped from "semantic token strings (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`)" to **"raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties, never a bare Chakra/theme token string"** — explicitly a house-style, not a correctness, requirement (`theme.colors`/`theme.space` *are* registered, so bare keys would resolve correctly). Type is the one exception: `textStyle="body2"` stays a bare key because there's no `var()` substitute for the composite expansion.

**Responsive.** Chakra's array shorthand (`['2xs','2xs','xs','xs']`) is now forbidden by rule — it would reintroduce bare keys. Recipes use explicit template-literal media queries keyed off `BP` from `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts`:

[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```
`footerShared.ts` is the "cross-file shared values stay in `theme/components/`" carve-out (breakpoints + `SIZE_COL_NAV`), and is the one place a recipe imports `foundation/` directly — media queries can't consume `var()`.

**Provisional values** are named constants at the top of the recipe with a comment containing `provisional`/`pending`/`placeholder`/`audit-allow:` — e.g. `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT`, `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT`, `SPACE_SECTION`. ## 3. Guards — `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (365 lines, new)

It walks the registered recipe map (`components` from `theme/components/index.ts`, plus the composed `theme`), recursively descending into nested media queries, pseudo-selectors and responsive containers, and asserts an empty offender list per rule.

Machinery worth knowing:
- `resolveAllBaseStyles` calls a **function-form `baseStyle` once per boolean prop combination** — `2^5 = 32` today (`inverse`, `disabled`, `hasError`, `focused`, `filled`). Exhaustive, not sampled, because a value can branch (`top: floated ? '3xs' : '50%'`) and `'3xs'` shipped precisely because the all-false default never reached it. Results are deduped by `where()`.
- `isResponsiveContainer` uses "are **ALL** keys breakpoints?" not "any" — because `xl`/`2xl` are keys in both `breakpoints` and `spacing`, and `sm`/`md`/`lg` are in both `breakpoints` and `fontSizes`.

**Six tests / five enforced rules:**
1. `collect() actually walks the registered recipes` — an anti-vacuity guard: asserts `components` is non-empty and `collect()` returns hits, so deleting the registry can't turn the file green.
2. **No sizing property uses a bare spacing key.** `width`/`height`/`boxSize`/`minW`… resolve through `theme.sizes`, which is deliberately unregistered — `width: 'xl'` reads Chakra's `36rem` and shipped a 576px icon.
3. **No typography property uses a bare scale key.** `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` × (own scale keys ∪ spacing keys). `fontWeight` is deliberately excluded (`medium` = 500 in both scales).
4. **No compound shorthand contains a bare scale key.** `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser. Splits on whitespace after masking `var(...)`.
5. **No override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale.** The house-style rule — `gap: 'xs'` and `color: 'text.inverse'` resolve *correctly* but are banned so every call site is an unambiguous zimm reference.
6. **No recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name.** `extendTheme` deep-merges, so `Footer` would inherit SFCC's `Footer`. Allow-list: `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']`. Everything else must be namespaced `Zimm*`.

**What it explicitly does NOT catch** (stated in its own SCOPE header):
- The same mistakes made as a **JSX prop or inline `sx` merge** — it only walks the registered recipe map. Catching that class would need `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` over JSX attributes.
- **Raw hex/px/rem/em literals** — that's a different, broader check owned by `npm run audit:tokens`, which has no CI gate.

## 4. Hooks and state

Five hooks, all in the flat `overrides/app/hooks/` directory (not co-located), all `use<Component><Feature>.ts`, all with a co-located test:

| Hook | Owns | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `useUiCopy.ts` | Nothing — `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY` | `{t, isLoading}` |
