input.prompt:
You are extracting a TESTABLE RUBRIC from three front-end engineering documents. Read each one IN FULL — do not skim or sample. They are moderate size (763, 807 and 792 lines).

FILES (read completely, in this order):
1. /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/uiBuild-knowledge.md
2. /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/fedBuild-manual.md
3. /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/fedLead-playbook.md

CONTEXT
These describe how UI should be built in a Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (Zimmermann, Chakra UI, TypeScript, an `overrides/` customisation layer over `@salesforce/retail-react-app`). They were revised 2026-08-25. I need to audit a specific feature branch against them.

YOUR OUTPUT — a numbered rubric, in two sections:

SECTION A — CHECKABLE RULES
Every rule that constrains how UI code is written, where each can be mechanically checked against a file. For each:
  - ID (R1, R2, ...)
  - RULE: one sentence, in your own words
  - PREDICATE: a concrete, checkable statement. Something a reviewer could evaluate as true/false against a given file — e.g. "a component's styling lives in a co-located <name>.css.ts registered in theme/components/index.ts, not in JSX props" — NOT a vague aspiration like "styling should be consistent".
  - SOURCE: which of the three docs, and the section heading it came from.

SECTION B — GUIDANCE (NOT CHECKABLE)
Rules that are real but cannot be reduced to a per-file predicate (process, judgement, estimation, team rhythm). Same fields minus PREDICATE. These must NOT be mixed into Section A — a rubric row that cannot be checked will produce a fake audit finding.

SECTION C — INTERNAL DISAGREEMENTS
Anywhere the three documents contradict each other, or where one says something a reader would reasonably interpret two ways. State both readings. Do not resolve them.

FOCUS the rubric on what an audit of a page-and-components feature branch would actually test:
- how a design value resolves (tokens, CSS custom properties, theme scales) and what fails silently
- component structure and the atom/molecule/organism split
- what an override does and does not intercept
- styling surface: recipes vs JSX props vs global classes
- data flow: container vs presentational, hooks, where fetching lives
- microcopy and content sourcing
- testing expectations per layer
- accessibility expectations
- Storybook expectations
- handling absent/unavailable data and design gaps

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- READ-ONLY. Do not write, create or modify any file.
- These documents are LOCAL-ONLY and must never be quoted at length or cited by filename in anything that could reach a git repository. In your report, paraphrase every rule in your own words. Cite source only as "uiBuild §N — <heading>" style short references so I can trace them locally. Never reproduce more than a short phrase verbatim.
- Do not evaluate any code in this pass. You are producing the measuring stick only, not measuring anything.
- If a rule appears in more than one document, state it once and list both sources.

Return the rubric as your final report. Be exhaustive on Section A — a missed rule is a missed audit finding.

REPO: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
PR #59 merged as commit `8362b3c` on `develop`. The pre-merge base is `cd68e97`.
Useful starting point: `git diff --name-status cd68e97 8362b3c -- overrides .claude` (94 commits of work).

READ (in full where small, representatively where large):
- overrides/app/components/footer/** (index.tsx, footer.css.ts, footerNavColumn/, bottomBar/)
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/** (atoms zimmButton, zimmIcon, zimmLogo, zimmModal, zimmNavItem, zimmTextInput; molecules zimmContactIconRow, zimmInputAction; organisms zimmSubscribeModal, zimmSubscribeSection)
- overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts, recipeGuards.test.ts, header.ts, listMenu.ts, footerShared.ts
- overrides/app/hooks/ (useUiCopy.ts, useSubscribeSection.*, useZimmModal.*, useCountryConfig.*, useContentfulClient.*)
- overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts, resolveByRegion.ts
- overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/**
- overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx
- .claude/rules/*.md  (these were revised by #59 — note what changed in them)

DOCUMENT each pattern under these headings. For every pattern give: what it is, at least one `file:line` citation, and how consistently it is applied (all sites / most / one-off).

1. STYLING SURFACE — where does styling live? co-located `<name>.css.ts` vs `theme/components/<name>.ts`; how recipes are registered; single-part vs multipart (`parts`); how variants/state are expressed; use of `var(--zimm-*)` vs bare Chakra token keys vs `textStyle`; any use of raw literals and how they are justified in comments.
2. COMPONENT STRUCTURE — the atom/molecule/organism split as actually practised; what qualifies for each tier; folder layout; export style (named vs default); props typing and where prop types live; JSDoc practice.
3. DATA FLOW — container vs presentational; which components call hooks; where fetching happens; how state is extracted into custom hooks and when; how props cross composition boundaries.
4. MICROCOPY & CONTENT — `useUiCopy` usage, key naming, fallback handling; when `useIntl` is used instead; how the two coexist.
5. TESTING — what gets a `*.test.ts(x)` vs a Storybook `play` vs both; how mocking is scoped; the `ZimmIcon` mock workaround; what `recipeGuards.test.ts` actually enforces (read the test body, list each guard); any vacuity/self-test guards.
6. STORYBOOK — story file structure, `title` categorisation actually used, named exports, when `play` is added, decorators, a11y handling.
7. ACCESSIBILITY — concrete practices visible in the code (aria attributes, focus handling, target sizes, semantics).
8. OVERRIDES — how #59 handles importing an already-overridden component; relative vs `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` paths; any comment explaining the resolver.
9. TOKENS — which foundation scales are registered vs not, and how the code compensates; where `var(--zimm-*)` is mandatory.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- READ-ONLY. Do not write, create or modify any file. Do not run git commands that mutate state (no checkout, no stash, no commit) — read-only git (`git show`, `git diff`, `git log`) is fine.
- Every claim needs a `file:line`. A claim you cannot cite must be labelled "UNCITED — inference".
- Where a pattern is applied inconsistently, say so explicitly and cite both the majority and the exception. Inconsistency is itself a finding I need.
- Do not read anything under /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/ outside the repo.

Return the pattern catalogue as your final report.

1. STYLING SURFACE — where styling lives for each component; recipe files and their shape; how they are registered; single-part vs multipart; how variants and state are expressed; token usage (`var(--zimm-*)`, bare keys, `textStyle`); any raw literals and how they are justified.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- READ-ONLY. Do not write, create or modify any file. Do not run mutating git commands (no checkout, stash, commit, add). Read-only git is fine.
- Every claim needs a `file:line`. Anything you cannot cite must be labelled "UNCITED — inference".
- Do not read anything under /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/ outside the repo.

**Four recipes exist, all co-located as `<name>.css.ts` beside their component.** No styling lives in `theme/components/<name>.ts`.

| Recipe | File | Shape |

**Consumption.** Single-part recipes are read via `useStyleConfig` and applied with `__css` on a `chakra.*` primitive: `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:20,23`; `zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:18,23`; `zimmProductContent/index.tsx:29,32`. The multipart recipe uses `useMultiStyleConfig` and reads `styles.root`/`styles.label`/`styles.value` at `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:27,32,33,40`.

**Token usage.**
- Inside `.css.ts` recipes, every colour and spacing value is a raw `var(--zimm-*)` custom property: `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` at `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:17`, `zimmProductDescription.css.ts:37`, `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:23`; `var(--zimm-scale-l)` at `zimmProductDescription.css.ts:32` and `zimmProductContent.css.ts:21`; `var(--zimm-scale-2xs)` at `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:22`. Both vars are real: `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:138` (`--zimm-scale-2xs`) and `:142` (`--zimm-scale-l`, = `spacing.l` = `1.25rem`/20px per `foundation/spacing.ts:14`).
- Inside `.tsx` component files, colour is a **bare Chakra key** on a JSX prop: `color="text.default"` at `zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23`. The distinction matches the enforcement boundary described at `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:37-43` — the bare-token guard *"walk[s] the registered recipe map only … they cannot see the same mistakes made as a JSX prop."*

All four keys are defined in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts:67,101,143,202`.
- On the page, spacing uses bare scale keys as JSX props: `<Stack spacing="l" paddingTop="l">` at `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:881`.

**Raw literals in recipes and how they are justified.** The only literals in the four recipes are zeroes — `margin: 0` (`zimmProductPrice.css.ts:16`, `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:26,30`), `marginBlock: 0` and `paddingInlineStart: 0` (`zimmProductDescription.css.ts:44,51`). Two named constants stand in for spacing values, each with a provenance comment:
- `SPACE_BETWEEN_BLOCKS` at `zimmProductDescription.css.ts:22-32`: *"Measured value: none — the DS specifies 20px within the text group … and says nothing about spacing between paragraphs inside the description itself. 20px (`spacing.l`) is carried over from that group rhythm rather than invented … Missing token: none — the value maps exactly onto `spacing.l`. Owner: UI designer, batched with the 28px / 44px gap questions."*
- `SPACE_WITHIN_TEXT_GROUP` at `zimmProductContent.css.ts:20-21`: *"DS: 20px between the name, price and description rows. Exactly `spacing.l`."*

Pixel literals do appear in **story decorators** (`width="218px"` at `zimmProductDescription/index.stories.tsx:23`, `zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx:29`; `width="218px" outline="1px dashed"` at `zimmProductName/index.stories.tsx:36`), justified as showing wrap behaviour at the real column width (`zimmProductName/index.stories.tsx:31-32`, `zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx:25-26`).

**Two documented "non-inventions" in the description recipe** (`zimmProductDescription.css.ts:11-19`): list markers stay off because *"Chakra's global reset already applies `:where(ol, ul) { list-style-type: none }` … That is restated explicitly here so the rendering does not silently change if the global registry is ever revised — it is not a design decision taken in this file"*; and no responsive inset, because *"nothing in the DS insets the description within that column, so nothing is added here."*

**A specificity decision is recorded twice.** `zimmProductDescription.css.ts:39-42`: *"Both rules below are deliberately written as `& > *`, not `& > p` / `& > ul`. An element-named selector is more specific than `& > * + *`, so the reset would win and the rhythm would never apply."* And `zimmProductContent.css.ts:6-18` explains choosing flex `gap` over `& > * + *`: *"An adjacent-sibling rule (`& > * + *`) was tried first and silently lost to the `margin: 0` in `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` and `zimmProductDescription.css.ts` — equal specificity, and Emotion happened to inject the child classes last. `gap` is set on the container and no child declaration can reach it."*

## 3. DATA FLOW

**Fetch** happens only at the page. `useProduct(...)` at `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:200-225` with the base `expand` list; the resolved product comes out of `useProductInventory(...)` at `:280-286`. None of the six new components calls a data hook.

**A dedicated mapper module sits between them**: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`. It exports `selectPdpProductInfo(product, priceData, currency, formatPrice)` at `:48-66`, plus four exported types — `PdpSourceProduct` (`:17-25`), `PdpSourcePrice` (`:28`), `FormatPrice` (`:31`), `PdpProductInfo` (`:33-39`). Its own header states why it is a separate file (`productInfo.ts:1-9`): *"Extracted from the page so the mapping is unit-testable on its own … a mis-keyed field here does not fail loudly: it falls through to `undefined`, the component returns `null`, and the page renders a plausible-looking product with one line quietly missing. Neither a Storybook `play` (which supplies its own props) nor an axe run can see that."*

Mapping rules, all at `productInfo.ts:54-65`: returns `null` when `!product?.name` (`:54`); price is formatted only when `typeof priceData?.currentPrice === 'number'`, else `''` (`:58`); `description ← longDescription` (`:59`); `modelInfo ← c_modelFit` (`:60`); `styleCode ← product.master?.masterId ?? product.id` (`:64`) with the reason written at `:61-63`: *"The style code shoppers see is the master style number. `product.id` is the variant SKU once a size is selected, so reading it would silently show a different value after the first swatch click."*

**Formatting is injected, not imported.** `FormatPrice` is a parameter type (`productInfo.ts:30-31`, *"Injected so this module stays free of react-intl"*); the page supplies it at `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:694-695` as `formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency: priceCurrency })`. The price atom itself does no formatting, documented at `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:5-10`: *"This atom does no formatting of its own so it stays usable from Storybook without an intl provider."*

**The page↔component boundary is a render-prop.** `ProductView` gains one new prop, `renderHeader`, typed at `product-view/index.tsx:153-163` and defaulted at `:267` to `(headerProps) => <ProductViewHeader {...headerProps} />`. It is invoked twice — once in the mobile block (`product-view/index.tsx:676-683`) and once in the desktop block (`:729-736`) — with the same six values (`name`, `product`, `priceData`, `currency`, `category`, `isProductPartOfBundle`). The prop doc states the purity requirement: *"ProductView renders the header twice (mobile and desktop breakpoints), so this is called twice with the same arguments. Keep it pure."* (`product-view/index.tsx:161-162`), restated at `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:705`.

The page supplies `renderStaticProductHeader` (`pages/product-detail/index.tsx:707-741`), passed only on the non-set/non-bundle branch (`:864`). Inside it, `selectPdpProductInfo(headerProduct ?? { name }, priceData, currency ?? '', formatPrice)` (`:715`) feeds `<ZimmProductContent name price description headingLevel="h2" />` (`:730`). The header also reproduces the base breadcrumb (`:719-723`) and promo callout (`:734-738`); the reason is at `:700-703`: *"The breadcrumb and promo callout are reproduced from the base header rather than dropped: `renderHeader` replaces the whole header block, and neither of those belongs to SFCC-89 (breadcrumb is SFCC-578, badges are SFCC-132/225), so losing them here would be a regression rather than a scope decision."*

**A second call site sits outside ProductView.** `staticInfo = selectPdpProductInfo(product, null, product?.currency ?? '', formatPrice)` at `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:745` (note `priceData` is `null` here), consumed at `:882-883` by `<ZimmProductModelInfo modelInfo={staticInfo?.modelInfo} />` and `<ZimmProductStyleCode value={staticInfo?.styleCode} />`, inside `<Stack spacing="l" paddingTop="l">` (`:881`) placed after `<InformationAccordion product={product} />` (`:879`). The positioning rationale is at `:743-744`.

Props cross composition boundaries by explicit pass-through only — `ZimmProductContent` forwards `name`/`headingLevel`/`price`/`description` to its three children at `zimmProductContent/index.tsx:33-35`. No context, no spread.

## 4. MICROCOPY & CONTENT

Exactly one user-facing literal string exists in the new components: the style-code label. It is sourced from the Contentful-backed copy hook, not a prop and not `react-intl`:

- `import { useUiCopy } from 'app/hooks/useUiCopy'` — `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:3`
- `const LABEL_FALLBACK = 'Style Code:'` — `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:6`, with the comment *"English fallback for useUiCopy() below — not a prop. Named so the string appears once, the same way zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx keeps its fallbacks."* (`:5-6`)
- `const { t } = useUiCopy()` — `:28`; `t('pdp.styleCodeLabel', LABEL_FALLBACK)` — `:33`

The choice is argued at `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:20-25`: *"The label is microcopy, so it comes from `useUiCopy()` rather than a prop: it is the same string for every caller, and the hook is Context-backed app-wide static content, which components.md explicitly allows a presentational leaf to read. With no UiCopyProvider mounted (Storybook, a unit test) it degrades to the fallback above, so this stays renderable with zero setup."* The hook's no-provider fallback behaviour is real — `overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts` defines `FALLBACK_ONLY` and `useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`.

All other visible text is product data from the API (name, price, description, model line, style code value). The `pdp.styleCodeLabel` key appears nowhere else in the repo — it is expected to exist as a Contentful `uiCopy` entry, not a repo file.

**Product copy is never treated as plain text** — description and model info both go through `parseRichText` (`zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:20`, `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:20`).

## 7. ACCESSIBILITY

- **Heading level is a required prop, never defaulted.** `as: 'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'` at `zimmProductName/index.tsx:12`, with the reason at `:7-11`: *"a silent `h1` default duplicates the base PDP's own screen-reader-only `<h1>Product Details</h1>`."* The page passes `headingLevel="h2"` and explains at `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:727-729`: *"h2, not h1: the page already emits a screen-reader-only `<h1>Product Details</h1>`, and the base header this replaces rendered the name as an h2. Changing the outline is SEO's call, not a side-effect of this ticket."* That `<h1>` is at `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:749-751`.
- **A real text node, not CSS, joins the style-code label and value.** `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:34-39`: *"A real space so `textContent` — what a screen reader reads out and what a shopper copies — is 'Style Code: 8637DS241' … It adds no visual width: a whitespace-only anonymous flex item is not rendered (CSS Flexbox §4), so the 4px `gap` in the recipe remains the only spacing."* Asserted at `zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx:19` and `index.stories.tsx:23`.
- **Semantic elements from the source markup are preserved rather than flattened.** `parseRichText` re-creates `p`/`ul`/`ol`/`li`/`strong`/`em`/`b`/`i`/`br` as real React elements (`utils/richText.tsx:28,31`), so list semantics survive even though markers are visually suppressed.
- **Optional lines collapse entirely instead of rendering empty nodes**, so no empty landmark/text node is exposed: `zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:19`, `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:19`, `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:29`.
- **Heading roles are asserted by role, not by tag**, in the `play` functions (`zimmProductName/index.stories.tsx:25,55`).
- Model info renders as `<Text as="div">` (`zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23`) rather than a `<p>`. UNCITED — inference: this avoids invalid `<p>` inside `<p>` nesting when `c_modelFit` contains block markup; no comment states this.

## 9. RICH TEXT / SANITISATION

`overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` (227 lines) exports four functions: `decodeEntities` (`:94`), `parseRichText` (`:115`), `richTextToPlainText` (`:215`), `isBlankRichText` (`:227`).

**How it works.** `parseRichText` runs a single regex (`TAG_RE`, `:68`) over the string, maintaining a stack of `Frame = { tag, children }` (`:106,118-120`). For each token: text between tags is decoded and pushed (`:126-133,143`); tags in `DROP_CONTENT_TAGS` open a depth-counted skip region so nested same-name tags close correctly (`:122-123,146-160`); closing tags unwind to the matching frame only if one exists, so a stray `</li>` is ignored (`:162-170`); `VOID_TAGS` become childless elements (`:172-175`); anything not in `ALLOWED_TAGS` is **unwrapped** — tag dropped, text kept (`:177`); unclosed tags are still closed at the end (`:185`). Elements are built with `React.createElement(frame.tag, { key }, children)` (`:194-200`) — **no attributes are ever passed through**, and no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` appears anywhere in the file.

Allow-lists: `ALLOWED_TAGS` = `p, ul, ol, li, strong, em, b, i` (`:28`); `VOID_TAGS` = `br` (`:31`); `DROP_CONTENT_TAGS` = `script, style, template, noscript, iframe, object, embed, svg` (`:38`); `VOID_ELEMENTS` = the full HTML void set (`:44-59`); `LIST_CONTAINERS` = `ul, ol` (`:62`). Reproduced on 2026-08-23: a PDP that returns 200 returns 500 with the import present, and the asset is never copied into `build/`, so a production bundle fails the same way. Needs raising with Integration before #57's dependency addition is accepted."*

**Why parse rather than sanitise-then-inject** — `richText.tsx:6-9`: *"This deliberately does not sanitise a string and hand it to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. It parses the markup and emits React nodes, so raw HTML is never injected: every text run goes through React's own escaping and every attribute is discarded. The worst case for a malformed or hostile input is that it renders as visible text, not that it executes."*

**Why the blank check is derived, not re-implemented** — `richText.tsx:206-213`: *"Derived by walking the output of `parseRichText` rather than re-stripping the string, so the two can never disagree about what counts as content … Business Manager can save a field as `<p></p>` or a bare `<br>`, which parses to real nodes but shows nothing, and rendering it would leave an empty box still contributing to the layout rhythm."* Implemented via `nodeText` (`:217-224`), which recurses through strings, arrays and valid elements' children.

## 1. STYLING SURFACE

**Four recipes exist, all co-located as `<name>.css.ts` beside their component.** No styling lives in `theme/components/<name>.ts`.

| Recipe | File | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `ZimmProductContent` | `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/zimmProductContent.css.ts:23-30` | single-part, `baseStyle` object only |

**Two components carry no recipe at all**, each justified in a JSDoc block:
- `ZimmProductName` — `zimmProductName/index.tsx:16-18`: *"No recipe: the whole spec is one `textStyle` plus a semantic colour token, which tiers 1-2 of .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md already cover."*

**Registration.** All four are imported and spread into the exported `components` map in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:13-16` (imports) and `:31-34` (map entries).

**Consumption.** Single-part recipes are read via `useStyleConfig` and applied with `__css` on a `chakra.*` primitive: `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:20,23`; `zimmProductDescription/index.tsx:18,23`; `zimmProductContent/index.tsx:29,32`. The multipart recipe uses `useMultiStyleConfig` and reads `styles.root`/`styles.label`/`styles.value` at `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:27,32,33,40`.

**Variants and state.** Only `ZimmProductPrice` declares a `variants` map, with a single populated key. The reason is written out at `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:3-13`: *"The DS models `pdp/price` with two states, so this carries a `variants` map rather than a bare `baseStyle` … Only `default` is populated: the was/now (sale) treatment belongs to SFCC-194 … Adding a `sale` key that merely echoes `default` would look finished and be wrong, so the extension point is documented instead of stubbed."* The prop type mirrors this: `variant?: 'default'` at `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:12`, annotated *"Reserved for SFCC-194's was/now treatment; only `default` is implemented today."* No component expresses hover/focus/active state.

**Token usage.**
- Inside `.css.ts` recipes, every colour and spacing value is a raw `var(--zimm-*)` custom property: `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` at `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:17`, `zimmProductDescription.css.ts:37`, `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:23`; `var(--zimm-scale-l)` at `zimmProductDescription.css.ts:32` and `zimmProductContent.css.ts:21`; `var(--zimm-scale-2xs)` at `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:22`. Both vars are real: `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:138` (`--zimm-scale-2xs`) and `:142` (`--zimm-scale-l`, = `spacing.l` = `1.25rem`/20px per `foundation/spacing.ts:14`).
- Inside `.tsx` component files, colour is a **bare Chakra key** on a JSX prop: `color="text.default"` at `zimmProductName/index.tsx:20` and `zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:23`. The distinction matches the enforcement boundary described at `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:37-43` — the bare-token guard *"walk[s] the registered recipe map only … they cannot see the same mistakes made as a JSX prop."*

All four keys are defined in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts:67,101,143,202`.
- On the page, spacing uses bare scale keys as JSX props: `<Stack spacing="l" paddingTop="l">` at `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:881`.

**Raw literals in recipes and how they are justified.** The only literals in the four recipes are zeroes — `margin: 0` (`zimmProductPrice.css.ts:16`, `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:26,30`), `marginBlock: 0` and `paddingInlineStart: 0` (`zimmProductDescription.css.ts:44,51`). **A specificity decision is recorded twice.** `zimmProductDescription.css.ts:39-42`: *"Both rules below are deliberately written as `& > *`, not `& > p` / `& > ul`. ## 9. RICH TEXT / SANITISATION

`overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` (227 lines) exports four functions: `decodeEntities` (`:94`), `parseRichText` (`:115`), `richTextToPlainText` (`:215`), `isBlankRichText` (`:227`).

**How it works.** `parseRichText` runs a single regex (`TAG_RE`, `:68`) over the string, maintaining a stack of `Frame = { tag, children }` (`:106,118-120`). For each token: text between tags is decoded and pushed (`:126-133,143`); tags in `DROP_CONTENT_TAGS` open a depth-counted skip region so nested same-name tags close correctly (`:122-123,146-160`); closing tags unwind to the matching frame only if one exists, so a stray `</li>` is ignored (`:162-170`); `VOID_TAGS` become childless elements (`:172-175`); anything not in `ALLOWED_TAGS` is **unwrapped** — tag dropped, text kept (`:177`); unclosed tags are still closed at the end (`:185`). Elements are built with `React.createElement(frame.tag, { key }, children)` (`:194-200`) — **no attributes are ever passed through**, and no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` appears anywhere in the file.

Allow-lists: `ALLOWED_TAGS` = `p, ul, ol, li, strong, em, b, i` (`:28`); `VOID_TAGS` = `br` (`:31`); `DROP_CONTENT_TAGS` = `script, style, template, noscript, iframe, object, embed, svg` (`:38`); `VOID_ELEMENTS` = the full HTML void set (`:44-59`); `LIST_CONTAINERS` = `ul, ol` (`:62`). Entity decoding covers 14 named entities plus decimal and hex numeric refs, rejecting out-of-range code points rather than throwing (`:70-104`).

**Why it exists rather than a library** — verbatim, `richText.tsx:11-19`:
> *"Why not `isomorphic-dompurify` — the engine the earlier SFCC-89 attempt on PR #57 adds as a production dependency: importing it anywhere in the SSR graph crashes the server render. webpack bundles jsdom into the server bundle but rewrites `__dirname`, so jsdom's module-scope `fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(__dirname, '../../../browser/default-stylesheet.css'))` resolves outside the project and throws ENOENT at import time, before `sanitize()` is ever called. Reproduced on 2026-08-23: a PDP that returns 200 returns 500 with the import present, and the asset is never copied into `build/`, so a production bundle fails the same way. Needs raising with Integration before #57's dependency addition is accepted."*

**Why parse rather than sanitise-then-inject** — `richText.tsx:6-9`: *"This deliberately does not sanitise a string and hand it to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. It parses the markup and emits React nodes, so raw HTML is never injected: every text run goes through React's own escaping and every attribute is discarded. The worst case for a malformed or hostile input is that it renders as visible text, not that it executes."*

**Why the blank check is derived, not re-implemented** — `richText.tsx:206-213`: *"Derived by walking the output of `parseRichText` rather than re-stripping the string, so the two can never disagree about what counts as content … Business Manager can save a field as `<p></p>` or a bare `<br>`, which parses to real nodes but shows nothing, and rendering it would leave an empty box still contributing to the layout rhythm."* Implemented via `nodeText` (`:217-224`), which recurses through strings, arrays and valid elements' children.

Two `/* c8 ignore next */` pragmas with reasons sit at `:191` and `:222`.

## SECTION C — INTERNAL DISAGREEMENTS AND TWO-WAY READINGS

**C1 — Is `var(--zimm-*)` in JSX required, or is any design value in JSX itself the violation?**
Reading A: the hierarchy was corrected so that raw CSS-custom-property references in JSX are now the *required* form; a bare token string is the finding and the fix is to rewrite it as `var()`. Reading B: the same sections state brand values mostly should not be in JSX at all, that `var()` in JSX is for a genuine prop-system gap only, and that the measured reality is exactly one such instance — under which reading a `var()` in JSX is itself a finding and the fix is to move the value into the recipe. The two named live violations (`color="text.default"` in two atoms) get different remedies depending on which reading applies. SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — [CORRECTED]; fedBuild §3 — [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted

**C2 — Is recipe co-location neutral, preferred, or a governance smell?**
Reading A: purely organisational — Chakra resolves by string key, so co-located or central is a free choice. Reading B: the folder layout and quick reference both prescribe a co-located `<name>.css.ts` as the standard shape. Reading C: co-location is a governance hazard, because the last-match-wins CODEOWNERS rule for `**/*.css.ts` silently drops the Tier 2 approver requirement that the surrounding directory carries — flagged as something nothing prevents for `_app-config/` or `seo/`. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — Styling surface / Co-location changes who reviews it; fedBuild §2, §13; fedLead — Last-match-wins

**C3 — 14 recipe files or 18?**
One doc measures `var(--zimm-*)` in 14 theme files on `develop` (10 co-located + 4 central), with 18 only in the uncommitted working tree. The other states 18 recipe files measured on `develop`. Both cite the same date and commit. An auditor using either as a baseline will get a different delta. SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — What survives from the old advice; fedBuild §3 — In practice this rarely arises

**C4 — Is `.scss` a permitted last resort or prohibited?**
Reading A: scoped `.scss` is rung 5 of the styling hierarchy — legitimate when `sx` genuinely cannot express something, with the rider "in practice: never". Reading B: styling is a registered recipe, always — explicitly not a plain stylesheet, with a structural argument (a stylesheet can only see the derived output at the bottom of the pipeline). SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — The styling hierarchy; uiBuild §3 — Styling surface

**C5 — Which vehicle expresses a prop-system gap: `sx`, or a JSX prop with `var()`?**
The hierarchy names `sx` as rung 4 for a one-off gap. The single sanctioned real-world instance is a conditional `paddingLeft` written as a JSX prop, not as `sx`. Whether a reviewer should require the gap to be expressed as `sx` or as a `var()`-valued prop is unstated, and the docs model each. SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — The styling hierarchy; uiBuild §1 — What survives from the old advice

**C6 — Tier is read off the imports, or off what the template renders?**
Reading A: read it off the imports, not the DOM. Reading B: tier by composition meaning what the component's own template renders. These diverge for a component that imports nothing but renders slotted ui-kit children, and for one that imports a ui-kit component it renders only conditionally. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — Tier is by composition; fedLead Play 1 — The atoms governance model

A3 is back; A1 and A2 still running. Two things from it worth flagging now, before synthesis:

**Our own documentation has a hole.** Of the four open items I've been reporting to you, only the `c_modelFit` one is actually written down in the code (three places). If this branch changed hands tomorrow, three of four known issues would be invisible.

**A tier discrepancy I'd missed.** `product-view/index.tsx:19` self-labels as *"Tier 2 (Shared Product Components, owner Squad B)"* — but `protectedFiles.md:29-35` lists `product-tile/`, `product-item/`, `display-price/`, `image-gallery/`, `swatch-group/`, `recommended-products/` and **not** `product-view/`. So either the comment asserts a governance status the repo doesn't actually confer, or the path is missing from the tier list. Either way it needs resolving before the PR, since it changes who has to approve.

# AUDIT RUBRIC — Zimmermann PWA Kit UI feature branch
Source shorthand: **uiBuild** = UI build knowledge doc · **fedBuild** = build manual · **fedLead** = lead playbook. All three revised 2026-08-25. Rules paraphrased throughout; nothing below is safe to assume is quotable.

---

## SECTION A — CHECKABLE RULES

### A1. How a design value resolves (tokens, CSS custom properties, theme scales)

**R1 — Sizing props never take a bare scale key**
PREDICATE: No JSX prop or recipe key in `width`, `height`, `boxSize`, `minWidth/maxWidth`, `minHeight/maxHeight` has a bare string scale key (`'xl'`, `'m'`, `'s'`, `'l'`, `'2xl'`…). It must be `var(--zimm-scale-*)` or an explicit unit value.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — The registration reality; fedBuild §3 — The trap: a spacing key on a sizing prop; fedLead Play 5 — The token checklist

**R2 — Typography props never take a bare scale key**
PREDICATE: No `fontSize`, `lineHeight` or `letterSpacing` anywhere in the diff carries a bare token key; typography is expressed via `textStyle` or an explicit `var(--zimm-*)` / unit value.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — The registration reality; fedBuild §3 — The trap

**R3 — Only `space` is a registered scale**
PREDICATE: Any assumption in the code that `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights` or `letterSpacings` resolve Zimmermann keys is absent; only `margin`/`padding`/`gap` families rely on bare-key resolution.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — The registration reality; fedBuild §3 — The trap

**R4 — Colour and spacing in JSX use the raw CSS custom property, not a bare theme token string**
PREDICATE: No JSX style prop uses a bare semantic token string (e.g. `color="text.default"`, `padding="m"`); where a design value must appear in JSX it is written as `var(--zimm-color-*)` / `var(--zimm-scale-*)`.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — [CORRECTED] var(--zimm-*) in component JSX is now required; fedBuild §3 — [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted

**R5 — `textStyle` is the sole legitimate bare key**
PREDICATE: The only bare token string in a `.tsx` is a `textStyle` value; every other bare key is a finding.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — [CORRECTED]; fedBuild §3 — [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted

**R6 — All text uses a registered text style**
PREDICATE: Every text-bearing element resolves its type through `textStyle="<one of the 22 registered styles>"`, not a hand-assembled `fontSize` + `lineHeight` + `fontWeight` set.
SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — The styling hierarchy (rung 1)

**R7 — `textStyle` expanding to literals is not a violation**
PREDICATE: A raw-literal finding in emitted CSS that traces back to a `textStyle` expansion is not counted as a token violation.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — [CORRECTED] (…and it can never emit one)

**R8 — Numeric scale aliases are class-only**
PREDICATE: No `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric alias (`025`, `700`, `1100`, `1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`, or any other numeric form) appears in a `.tsx` or a recipe file; they appear only in global class definitions.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — Value equality is not token equality (check 3)

**R9 — Derived token files are never hand-edited**
PREDICATE: The diff does not modify `zimmTokens.ts` or any other derived output of the foundation → tokens → CSS-var pipeline.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — The pipeline is one-way

**R10 — Foundation is untouched**
PREDICATE: No file under `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` appears in the diff.
SOURCE: fedBuild §11 — Hard stops (3); fedBuild §13 — Quick reference

**R11 — No invented tokens or raw design literals**
PREDICATE: No raw hex, `px`, `rem` or `em` literal appears in component or recipe code without either being a registered token reference, or a named constant whose comment contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or `audit-allow: <reason>`.
SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — You don't add tokens; fedBuild §9 — Self-check; fedLead Play 5 — The token checklist

**R12 — Unit discipline**
PREDICATE: Type and spacing values are in `rem`; hairline geometry (border widths, focus-ring offsets) is in `px`; `em` appears only in breakpoint definitions or a genuinely context-relative case.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — Units; uiBuild §9 — 1.4.4 / 1.4.10

**R13 — Sub-pixel letter-spacing carries its px trace**
PREDICATE: Any `letterSpacing` rem value that does not round cleanly has a trailing comment giving the intended px value.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — Units

**R14 — A literal→token substitution passes all three equality checks**
PREDICATE: Every literal replaced by a token in the diff has (a) the same unit family, (b) the same semantic scale (spacing value → spacing token, sizing → sizing), and (c) a permitted target (not a numeric alias).
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — Value equality is not token equality

**R15 — No value is typed twice**
PREDICATE: No value in the diff is declared in more than one place — no new mirror/alias module of the token layer, no `sx` block reconstructing what a registered `textStyle` or recipe already provides.
SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — The real invariant is single-sourcing

**R16 — Icon, action and motion values are imported constants, not theme keys**
PREDICATE: `iconSizes`, `actionSizes` and `motion` are imported from `app/theme/foundation` and used directly (e.g. `boxSize={iconSizes.lg}`); they are never referenced as Chakra scale keys or bare strings.

**R30 — Interaction state lives in CSS pseudo-props**

**R34 — Styling lives in a registered recipe**

## SECTION B — GUIDANCE (NOT CHECKABLE PER FILE)

**G1 — Figma stays open for the whole build**, not consulted at the end. SOURCE: fedBuild §1 — Figma stays open the whole time

**G2 — Verify the Jira card's Figma link points at your frame** before building; a stale link propagates to BA sign-off and QA. Ask the BA to fix the card rather than resolving it in a DM. SOURCE: fedBuild §1; fedLead Play 8

**G3 — Text-node vs frame comparability is a judgement call.** Text nodes report a cap-height box and are not comparable to a CSS line box; frames and instances are. A uniform residual across siblings is measurement; a varying one is a defect. SOURCE: uiBuild §5 — The discriminator is node type; fedBuild §3 — Figma comparison

**G4 — Never cross-compare the two Figma files** (design system vs composed page states). SOURCE: uiBuild §5 — There are two Figma files; fedBuild §1

**G5 — Layout measurement method**: subtract non-component bands before comparing totals; isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM mutation one candidate at a time; measure `y` relative to the component root; use `domcontentloaded` not `networkidle`; dismiss the consent banner first; mutation-test layout fixes at mobile. SOURCE: uiBuild §5 — Measurement method

**G6 — A solution window measured in single pixels is a coincidence, not a tolerance** — treat it as a signal the constraint set is over-determined. SOURCE: uiBuild §6

**G7 — Compare widths, not `document.fonts.check()`**, when validating font loading; the fallback stack renders ~13% wider. SOURCE: uiBuild §5 — Type metrics

**G8 — The reuse ladder is a judgement sequence**: use as-is → override → compose existing atoms → build new. Rung 4 is rarest and needs justification. Check the registry and grep `ui-kits/` first. SOURCE: fedBuild §1; fedLead Play 1

**G9 — Check what the base already does before scoping** — a ticket claiming an integration is in scope may be describing a call the base already makes. SOURCE: fedBuild §1

**G10 — Run the propagation grep before scoping any "override X and it propagates" story.** SOURCE: uiBuild §4 — The generalised check; fedLead Play 1

**G11 — Copy-first requires a human confirmation stop** — prepare the overrides, add temporary markers, and wait for the user to confirm they render before making functional changes. SOURCE: fedBuild §2 — The copy-first rule

**G12 — Build in Storybook, not in the running app.** SOURCE: fedBuild §5

**G13 — A blank icon in Storybook is usually a sourcing signal**, not a broken glyph — base-template SVGs are ignore-loaded. SOURCE: fedBuild §5

**G14 — Three-surface self-review before opening the PR**: the diff, the MRT preview environment, and Figma side by side at mobile and desktop. SOURCE: fedBuild §9; fedLead Play 5

**G15 — Run local CodeRabbit before the PR** — required by AGENTS.md, verified by nothing. Use judgement on whether a finding is worth fixing now. SOURCE: fedBuild §9

**G16 — Reply in-thread to every CodeRabbit finding, fixed or not.** A fix commit with no reply teaches the bot nothing. When declining, name the specific rule or doc. Never accept its offer to open a GitHub issue. Cite the PRD line correctly the first time. SOURCE: fedBuild §10

**G17 — Conform to an unconditionally-worded repo rule even for a provable no-op**, adding an inline note; never argue "the rationale isn't engaged". SOURCE: fedBuild §10

**G18 — Escalation routing**: missing token → UI designer; ambiguous requirement → BA with doc citation; missing/stale Figma → BA; shared hook signature → RFC; new package → Integration; Tier 1 file → verified-session exception path; content model change → Integration/SI; anything spanning two tiers → stop. One question at a time. SOURCE: fedBuild §8; fedLead Play 9

**G19 — The 30-minute / 20-minute stuck rule** — ask in the group chat, or change approach; don't push harder. SOURCE: fedBuild §1; fedLead §3 — Shipping discipline

**G20 — Make a check fail on purpose before its pass counts.** A green check never proven capable of going red carries no information. Mutation testing proves a check *can* fail, not that it fails for the right reason. SOURCE: uiBuild §10 — The integrity principle; fedLead Play 5b

**G21 — Verify claims before acting**: absence in an extracted spec is not a decision; a codebase value isn't a spec until you find its source; ask for the Figma node, not a screenshot; value-matching audits produce confident nonsense; a grep count is not a coverage verdict. SOURCE: fedLead Play 5b

**G22 — Don't take an agent's report at face value.** The check is cheap; the propagation cost is not. SOURCE: fedLead §4

**G23 — The audit-loop diagnostic**: ask where a finding came from. If its origin is your own freshly-written code rather than a spec, a reproduced failure or a review comment, it is probably not the next thing to do. Ban "it's good practice" as a justification. Read the review queue before a self-directed pass. SOURCE: fedLead §4

**G24 — Present verdicts, don't auto-fix.** Offer the self-generated group rather than doing it. SOURCE: fedLead §4

**G25 — The authorisation ladder: investigate ≠ fix ≠ commit.** Change → verify → stop and show the diff → wait. Resuming from a summary is not an instruction to commit. SOURCE: fedLead §4; fedBuild §11 — Hard stops (11)

**G26 — Shipping discipline**: deploy first; partial-but-hardened beats complete-but-broken; descope rather than cut quality. SOURCE: fedLead §3

**G27 — Define done.** "Improve the footer" has no terminal state. SOURCE: fedLead §3

**G28 — Polishing is procrastination** — an edit that didn't change what someone can or can't do wasn't a real edit. SOURCE: fedLead §3

**G29 — Estimation re-baseline**: pages go down, components go up by more. Split component-build from page-composition effort. Challenge list: `Origin = Base`? already in ui-kits? content type needed (= second story)? Figma signed off? integration wired? data on the demo tiers? multi-site? SOURCE: fedLead Play 2

**G30 — Configuration variant vs composition variant** must be settled at story time; Contentful sync is additive-only so a wrongly-modelled variant is semi-permanent. SOURCE: fedLead Play 3

**G31 — The renderer contract**: one field-ID table identical in both stories of a Contentful pair; you own the template, the BA fills it, you sign off the IDs. Studio Experiences inverts the order — the review point moves to the prop type. SOURCE: fedLead Play 4

Slice by data source, split where risk differs, every story a vertical slice, quarantine later-sprint work, offer sub-tasks not more stories, check the ticket against the PRD. SOURCE: fedLead — Sprint, story and Jira/Confluence

**G42 — Confluence/`.docs` boundary**: source-of-truth or requirement → `.docs/`; how-to or human process doc → Confluence. SOURCE: fedLead — Confluence

## SECTION C — INTERNAL DISAGREEMENTS AND TWO-WAY READINGS

**C1 — Is `var(--zimm-*)` in JSX required, or is any design value in JSX itself the violation?**
Reading A: the hierarchy was corrected so that raw CSS-custom-property references in JSX are now the *required* form; a bare token string is the finding and the fix is to rewrite it as `var()`. Reading B: the same sections state brand values mostly should not be in JSX at all, that `var()` in JSX is for a genuine prop-system gap only, and that the measured reality is exactly one such instance — under which reading a `var()` in JSX is itself a finding and the fix is to move the value into the recipe. The two named live violations (`color="text.default"` in two atoms) get different remedies depending on which reading applies. SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — [CORRECTED]; fedBuild §3 — [CORRECTED] Rung 2 inverted

**C2 — Is recipe co-location neutral, preferred, or a governance smell?**
Reading A: purely organisational — Chakra resolves by string key, so co-located or central is a free choice. Reading B: the folder layout and quick reference both prescribe a co-located `<name>.css.ts` as the standard shape. Reading C: co-location is a governance hazard, because the last-match-wins CODEOWNERS rule for `**/*.css.ts` silently drops the Tier 2 approver requirement that the surrounding directory carries — flagged as something nothing prevents for `_app-config/` or `seo/`. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — Styling surface / Co-location changes who reviews it; fedBuild §2, §13; fedLead — Last-match-wins

**C3 — 14 recipe files or 18?**
One doc measures `var(--zimm-*)` in 14 theme files on `develop` (10 co-located + 4 central), with 18 only in the uncommitted working tree. The other states 18 recipe files measured on `develop`. Both cite the same date and commit. An auditor using either as a baseline will get a different delta. SOURCE: uiBuild §1 — What survives from the old advice; fedBuild §3 — In practice this rarely arises

**C4 — Is `.scss` a permitted last resort or prohibited?**
Reading A: scoped `.scss` is rung 5 of the styling hierarchy — legitimate when `sx` genuinely cannot express something, with the rider "in practice: never". Reading B: styling is a registered recipe, always — explicitly not a plain stylesheet, with a structural argument (a stylesheet can only see the derived output at the bottom of the pipeline). SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — The styling hierarchy; uiBuild §3 — Styling surface

**C5 — Which vehicle expresses a prop-system gap: `sx`, or a JSX prop with `var()`?**
The hierarchy names `sx` as rung 4 for a one-off gap. The single sanctioned real-world instance is a conditional `paddingLeft` written as a JSX prop, not as `sx`. Whether a reviewer should require the gap to be expressed as `sx` or as a `var()`-valued prop is unstated, and the docs model each. SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — The styling hierarchy; uiBuild §1 — What survives from the old advice

**C6 — Tier is read off the imports, or off what the template renders?**
Reading A: read it off the imports, not the DOM. Reading B: tier by composition meaning what the component's own template renders. These diverge for a component that imports nothing but renders slotted ui-kit children, and for one that imports a ui-kit component it renders only conditionally. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — Tier is by composition; fedLead Play 1 — The atoms governance model

**C7 — Is a11y covered by CI or is it manual-review territory?**
All three docs correct the earlier claim and state the a11y gate exists and runs. Two of them add, in the same breath, that it has never been made to fail on purpose and is therefore unproven, and one lists it under "already mechanical — don't spend review time here" while simultaneously recommending a deliberate break to find out whether it works. An auditor can reasonably treat a11y as gated (skip it) or as unverified (test it manually). SOURCE: uiBuild §10 — [CORRECTED] What is and is not gated; fedBuild §6 — [CORRECTED]; fedLead Play 5

**C8 — Is `alt=""` for decorative images settled or an open decision?**
Reading A: settled — `alt=""` for decorative is stated as the rule in the a11y patterns, the build manual's ast-grep section, and the renderer-contract field table (empty string permitted for decorative). Reading B: explicitly open — whether missing alt text should be *absent* or `alt=""` is named as a content-model question awaiting a decision from a named person. SOURCE: uiBuild §9; fedBuild §6; fedLead Play 4 vs fedLead Play 6 — Open item

**C9 — Does the shared Contentful hook hardcode `include`, or accept it?**
One doc says the shared hook builds a URL with `content_type`, `access_token` and `include`, implying a caller-supplied depth. The other says the footer passes `include: 3` *where the shared hook hardcodes `include=2`* — which cannot both be true of the same call path. Whether a new consumer can raise its own depth, or must work around a hardcoded 2, is undetermined. SOURCE: uiBuild §8 — Fetch-depth / Locale is not passed; fedBuild §7 — Fetch depth is load-bearing

**C10 — Is the static-content-hook exception a closed list or a category?**
The exception is phrased as "Context-backed, app-wide static-content hooks" with `useIntl` and `useUiCopy` in parentheses. Reading A: those two hooks only. Reading B: any hook meeting the stated criteria (Provider above the route tree, content identical for every consumer regardless of route) qualifies. An auditor will accept or reject a third such hook differently. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — One documented exception; fedBuild §1 — The one exception

**C11 — Who owns loading and error state?**
Reading A: components under `components/` receive data as props and do not fetch — so loading/error belong to the page or container. Reading B: every component that renders fetched data needs loading, error and absent states specified. A presentational leaf cannot know it is loading unless a prop tells it, and the docs don't say which layer holds the state. SOURCE: fedBuild §1 — Static-first; uiBuild §3; fedLead §3 — Three states are AC

**C12 — Do pages need Storybook stories?**
Reading A: every component exported from its folder needs a story; `Pages/` is one of the seven story categories, implying page-level stories are expected. Reading B: no page has a story today, despite a rules file requiring one for page-level assemblies — recorded as a live gap, not as a branch-blocking requirement. A page-and-components branch is affected directly. SOURCE: fedBuild §5 — Storybook / Categorisation; fedLead Play 7

**C13 — Do directly-imported foundation constants violate the no-design-values-in-JSX principle?**
`iconSizes`, `actionSizes` and `motion` are prescribed as imported constants used directly in JSX props (`boxSize={iconSizes.lg}`), which places a resolved design value in JSX and bypasses `var()` entirely. Reading A: a sanctioned exception, because these deliberately are not registered scales. Reading B: an inconsistency with both the "brand values shouldn't be in JSX" principle and the `var()` requirement, which the docs do not reconcile. SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — Icon, action and motion values are constants vs fedBuild §3 — [CORRECTED] Rung 2

**C14 — Do provisional foundation values need call-site acknowledgement?**
Motion values are flagged as provisional pending designer sign-off, and separately any placeholder value must carry a `provisional`/`pending`/`placeholder` comment to be downgraded by the token audit. Reading A: the provisional marker lives in the foundation file and consumers need no comment. Reading B: any consumption of a provisional value should carry the acknowledgement comment at the point of use. The same tension applies to the provisional button heights that disagree with the action-size tokens. SOURCE: fedBuild §3 — Icon, action and motion values / You don't add tokens; fedLead Play 9

**C15 — Is `ui-kits` a sanctioned kebab-case exception?**
The camelCase rule is stated as applying to all Zimmermann-authored directories, with kebab-case reserved for files mirroring Salesforce. `ui-kits` itself is kebab-cased and is explicitly named as an undocumented, unsettled exception, with a warning that leaving it undocumented invites further kebab directories. An auditor cannot tell from the docs whether kebab-cased subdirectories under `ui-kits/` are a violation. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — Placement; fedBuild §2; fedLead open items 7b, 7c

The eleven overridden directories include `foundation`, while a hard stop forbids modifying `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`. A reader can take `foundation` in that list as a components-level directory that is fair game, or as the theme foundation that is absolutely off-limits. The docs never disambiguate the two. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — What is actually overridden; fedBuild §2 — What's actually overridden vs fedBuild §11 — Hard stops (3)

`button` appears in the eleven overridden directories; separately, the central `theme/components/button.ts` is stated to no longer exist because the app-wide `Button` recipe is now keyed from a co-located file inside `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`, and `Button` is one of three sanctioned deliberate merges. SOURCE: uiBuild §3 — What is actually overridden / Co-location changes who reviews it; fedBuild §2

**C18 — The named styling authority is also flagged as unreliable.**
Two of the three docs declare a specific rules file the winning authority on styling if they disagree with it. The third documents that the same file references a companion doc that does not exist, is orphaned from the entry-point doc and invisible to the assistant tooling, and contains at least one rationale that the lead playbook records as simply untrue. An auditor is told both to defer to it and to distrust it. SOURCE: fedBuild header — Authority on styling; fedLead header; uiBuild §11 — overrideStyling.md is orphaned; fedLead open item 7

The docs instruct importing from `storybook/test` and reaching into `document` for portalled content, both of which contradict the repo's own testing rules file — described as documentation defects rather than code defects. A reviewer working from the repo rules will flag compliant code, and vice versa. Nothing in the three docs says the rules file has been amended. SOURCE: fedBuild §5, §9; uiBuild §10 — Harness traps

3. **`no typography property uses a bare scale key`** (line 305) — `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` map (lines 153-157) covering `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing`, each against its own Zimmermann keys ∪ spacing keys. `fontWeight` is deliberately excluded because `medium` resolves to 500 in both scales (lines 149-151).
4. **`no compound shorthand contains a bare scale key`** (line 315) — for `padding`/`margin`/`inset`/`gap`/`p`/`m` only (`SPACE_SHORTHANDS`, line 160), splits the value on whitespace *outside* `var(...)` (line 321) and flags any part that is a spacing key. Catches `padding: 'xs 0'`, which the browser drops entirely.
5. **`no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale`** (line 331) — the **house-style** guard, over `SPACE_PROPS` (44 entries, lines 70-113) and `COLOR_PROPS` (8 entries, line 116) against `SPACING_KEYS` and a recursively-flattened dotted `COLOR_KEYS` set (lines 60-66). Explicitly **not** a correctness bug (lines 28-34, 339-343): `space` and `colors` are registered, so the bare key resolves fine — it enforces `var(--zimm-*)` at every call site so reviewers don't have to consult the registered-scale list.
6. **`no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name`** (line 347) — since `extendTheme` deep-merges, a recipe named `Footer` would inherit SFCC's `Footer`. Compares each recipe's own `baseStyle` keys against the composed `theme.components[name]` keys; any key present after composition that wasn't declared came from the base. `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` (line 351) is the allow-list — everything else must be namespaced, which is why the recipes are `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmFooterNavColumn`, `ZimmFooterBottomBar` and not `Footer`.

**Self-declared blind spots**, written into the file header (lines 36-43): the walk sees the recipe map only, so it cannot catch the same mistakes as a JSX prop. Two live instances are named — `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) and a former bare `paddingLeft: '2xs'` in `footerNavColumn/index.tsx`'s inline `sx` merge that "was only found by a manual grep".

**5.5 Other vacuity/anchoring guards.**
- `footer/index.stories.tsx:231-237` — anchors both operands of a before/after height comparison above zero, with the reasoning that `display:none`, `height:0`, and jsdom all measure 0 twice and would satisfy the equality vacuously.
- `footer/index.stories.tsx:113-117` — reads `document.body.style.overflow` before the modal opens and asserts it is *not already* `hidden`, so the scroll-lock assertion can't pass trivially.
- `footer/index.stories.tsx:255-259` — rounds `getBoundingClientRect` to 1dp to avoid sub-pixel jitter failing a genuine no-shift.
- `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:81-84` — asserts every declared `parts` entry is actually produced by `baseStyle`.
- `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:41-46` — tests the *empty-and-focused* case specifically, because focus and filled resolve to the same colour in the light palette and only that case distinguishes "the focus branch ran" from "fell through to default".
- `useZimmModal.test.tsx:1-22` — a synthetic `TrapHarness` (line 46) exists solely for two branches no story can reach: the `!el.hasAttribute('disabled')` filter, and restoring a *non-empty* prior `overflow` value (`PRE_EXISTING_OVERFLOW = 'scroll'`, line 32).
- `fontFace.test.tsx:4-13` — pins three `assetRoot` branches after a real incident where every font URL lost its bundle prefix.
- `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:12-15` — keeps `beforeEach`/`afterEach` purely to match `.claude/rules/testing.md` as written, and says so.

**5.6 Test file conventions.** Fixture *builders* over literal blobs (`footer/index.test.tsx:36-58`, `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx:23-35`, `uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx:18-21`, `resolveByRegion.test.ts:9-14`); `test.each` tables for pure predicates (`safeHref.test.ts:10-40`); `vi.clearAllMocks()` in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` (`footer/index.test.tsx:141`, `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx:79`, `uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx:30`, `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:23`); `renderHook` for hooks (`useSubscribeSection.test.ts:7`, `useUiCopy.test.tsx:8`, `uiCopyProvider/index.test.tsx:25`). `.tsx` extension for a hook test is justified where a component mount is needed (`useZimmModal.test.tsx:20-21`).

## 7. ACCESSIBILITY

**7.1 Landmark and dialog semantics.** `<chakra.footer role="contentinfo">` (`footer/index.tsx:91`); `role="presentation"` backdrop + `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby aria-describedby` panel (`zimmModal/index.tsx:51-57`), with the ids supplied by the consumer and matched to real elements (`zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:58-59,63,78`).

**7.2 Never render a false affordance.** A control that cannot act is a non-interactive element, not a disabled button — applied twice with the same reasoning (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4): the locale placeholder renders as a `<div>` (`bottomBar/index.tsx:40-45`, and `bottomBar.css.ts:103-107` withholds `cursor`/`_focusVisible` to match), and an unusable contact channel renders as a labelled `<span>` (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:76-88`). The two comments cross-reference each other.

**7.3 Perceivable-but-inert.** The fallback span keeps the icon labelled rather than `aria-hidden`, so the channel is announced — the comment at `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:81-83` records that a previous `aria-hidden` caused WCAG 1.1.1 information loss.

**7.4 Icon aria is enforced at the type level.** `ZimmIconProps` is a discriminated XOR: `{'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never} | {'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string}` (`zimmIcon/index.tsx:93`), and `role="img"` is emitted only when a label is present (`zimmIcon/index.tsx:151`). Every decorative use passes `aria-hidden={true}` explicitly: `bottomBar/index.tsx:49`, `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:116`, `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:73`, `zimmButton/index.tsx:51`. **All sites.**

**7.5 Cross-origin links.** `target="_blank"` + explicit `rel="noopener noreferrer"` + a WCAG 3.2.5 accessible-name suffix, applied by scheme rather than by channel name (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:37,39-40,66-70`); `tel:`/`mailto:` deliberately get neither.

**7.6 Focus visibility.** `_focusVisible` with `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` (light) or a `--zimm-color-text-inverse` outline (dark), plus `outlineOffset`, in every interactive recipe: `zimmButton.css.ts:33-37,82-86,113-117,143-147,168-172,192-196`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts:58-62,66-70`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:156-162`, `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:27-31`, `footer.css.ts:135-139`. The footer wordmark button's reset exists specifically to restore the ring the anchor-less markup would lack (`footer.css.ts:126-128`). `zimmButton.css.ts:28-32` records that the previous `outline:none` + background swap was an actual WCAG 2.4.7 failure (`#191919` vs `#000000`).

**7.7 Target size (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, 24px).** `zimmTextInput.css.ts:151-154` (`minWidth`/`minHeight`), `zimmButton.css.ts:226-240` (`minW`/`minH` on the `icon` size — with the note that Chakra's `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0` as a style prop so any `p` here is silently discarded), `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:11,21-22`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts:20-23` (`minHeight` as a floor, not a fixed height, so wrapped labels grow).

**7.8 Form semantics.** `htmlFor`/`id` pairing via `useId` (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:69-71,93,97`), `aria-invalid`, computed `aria-describedby` joining helper+error ids (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:107-108`), `role="alert"` on the error paragraph (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:127`) and on the subscribe failure message (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:76`), `aria-live="polite"` on the subscribe state slot (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:62`), `autoComplete="email"` when `type==='email'` (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:103`).

**7.9 Dialog keyboard mechanics** live in `useZimmModal.ts`: focus save/restore around open/close (lines 48-63), body-scroll lock restoring the *previous* value (lines 66-73), Escape (line 78), and a Tab trap with a third branch for focus that has escaped the boundary entirely — WCAG 2.1.2, cited at lines 96-102.

**7.10 Semantic markup choices are argued in comments, not assumed.** `<ul>`/`<li>` for nav links with `display:flex` on the `<li>` and the 1.5px line-box measurement behind it (`footerNavColumn.css.ts:63-69`); the contact row placed as the *last child of the list* rather than a sibling (`footerNavColumn/index.tsx:84-88`); a `<button>` rather than `<a href>` for the wordmark to mirror the header (`footer/index.tsx:120-124`); `aria-label="Zimmermann home"` at line 125; `role="img"` + `aria-label` on the inline logo SVG (`zimmLogo/index.tsx:30-31`).

**7.11 Contrast is reasoned about in the recipe.** `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts:14-15` — `text.secondary` (#666, 5.74:1) chosen over `text.muted` (#969696), which "would fail WCAG AA 4.5:1 at 12px on the white modal panel". `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:55-58` — failure copy uses the coral inverse error colour so it doesn't read as success.

**7.12 Units are chosen for zoom (WCAG 1.4.4).** `footer.css.ts:6-9`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:27-35` (a px `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT` broke a rem-derived slot at 200% zoom — reserved 90px against a 53px field), `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:10-11`.

## 9. TOKENS

**9.1 Registered as Chakra scales:** `borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space` (from `spacing`), `textStyles`, `components` — `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:51-62`.

**9.2 Deliberately NOT registered, with the collision table in-file:** `fontSizes`, `transition`, `sizes` — `overrides/app/theme/index.ts:31-39`. Reason: identical key names, different values, ~199 base call sites. `foundation/sizes.ts:3-7` repeats it for `iconSizes` ("Chakra's `sizes.lg` is 32rem"). Compensation is stated at `theme/index.ts:41-44`: use `textStyle` for type; import the constants directly for motion/icon/action dimensions.

**9.3 `var(--zimm-*)` is MANDATORY — not merely preferred — on any property that resolves through an unregistered scale.** Three comment sites say this in the imperative and give the failure mode:
- `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:12-16` — "**MUST** be the CSS var, not the bare token key `'xl'` … Chakra's default `sizes.xl` is 36rem (576px) — which blew each icon up to 576px and destroyed the whole footer layout. Same rule applies to `boxSize`/`min`/`maxWidth`/`Height`."
- `zimmTextInput.css.ts:127` — `height: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)'`, "var, not `'l'`: theme.sizes has no `'l'` key"; and `:152` — "var, not `'xl'`: min-width/height resolve via theme.sizes (xl = 36rem), not theme.space".
- `zimmButton.css.ts:233-235` — same rule, cross-referencing `zimmTextInput` as "the sibling control in the same trailing slot".

**9.4 On *registered* scales, `var(--zimm-*)` is mandatory as house style rather than for correctness,** and is machine-enforced — `recipeGuards.test.ts:331-345` plus `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:16-27`.

**9.5 Media queries are the one sanctioned place foundation values are imported directly rather than referenced via `var()`,** because media queries cannot consume custom properties: `theme/components/footerShared.ts:9-17` imports `breakpoints.md` from `../foundation/gridSystem` and carries an `audit-allow:` note that the raw `em` is "correct and permanent here, not a placeholder awaiting a token". `BP.tabletWide` (53.75em) and `BP.desktop` (64em) have no foundation equivalent, and `desktop` deliberately differs from Chakra `lg`=62em / `xl`=80em (lines 20-21).

**9.6 A concrete colour value (not a `var()`) is required where the consumer is an SVG attribute** — `useToken('colors', ['text.inverse','text.default'])` at `zimmLogo/index.tsx:23`, with the reason at lines 21-22: "an SVG `fill` attribute needs a concrete colour value, not a custom-property reference." **One-off.**

**9.7 Missing foundation entries are compensated by a named local constant, never a bare literal, and are always labelled with the owner.** See §1.7. The standing gaps recorded: no element-level opacity token (`zimmButton.css.ts:7-11`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:37-38`), no inverse focus-ring var (`zimmButton.css.ts:4-5`), no `4.5px` spacing entry (`zimmNavItem.css.ts:9-10`), no field-height token (`zimmTextInput.css.ts:26`), no modal-size token (`zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:11-13`), no logo size tokens (`zimmLogo/index.tsx:9-11`), 48px available only as the numeric alias `--zimm-scale-1200` and not as a named key (`header.ts:57-58`, `footer.css.ts:6-9`).

**9.8 Numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases exist but are the non-preferred surface.** `theme/index.ts:47-49` — "duplicates of the named scale (400 = 16px = `m`) … exist only for the `.zimm-*` global classes; the named scale is the Chakra-facing surface." Used anyway where the named key doesn't exist: `header.ts:59` (`--zimm-scale-1200`), `listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84` (`--zimm-scale-700`).

**9.9 Fonts moved from "fallback-only" to self-hosted in this PR.** Two `.woff2` added under `overrides/app/static/fonts/`; declared by `overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx:54-69` via a raw Emotion `<Global>` (Chakra's style processor mangles quoted font-family stacks — `fontFace.tsx:17-19`, matching the same note at `theme/index.ts:21-24`); mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and `.storybook/preview.tsx` so app and Storybook cannot drift (`fontFace.tsx:20-22`). `assetRoot` deliberately reimplements two lines of `getAssetUrl` rather than importing it, with the bundling reason at `fontFace.tsx:27-40`. Only two faces because all 22 textStyles resolve to weight 400 or 500 and `fonts.body === fonts.heading` (`fontFace.tsx:14-16`). `foundation/fonts.ts:1-3` was rewritten from "not self-hosted — the Monotype licence forbids it" to "IS self-hosted", and `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md:27-47` was rewritten accordingly, including an explicit retraction ("an earlier revision of this section claimed there was [an environment gate]").

**5.4 `recipeGuards.test.ts` — what it actually enforces (six tests).** File: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`.

Mechanism first: `collect()` (line 263) iterates `Object.entries(components)` — the registered recipe map — and for each recipe walks `resolveAllBaseStyles(r)` plus `r.variants` and `r.sizes` (lines 267-272) with a recursive `walk` (line 191) that descends media queries, pseudo-selectors and responsive containers, carrying the nearest enclosing property name forward. `isResponsiveContainer` (line 181) requires **all** keys to be breakpoints, load-bearing because `xl`/`2xl`/`sm`/`md`/`lg` are keys in both `breakpoints` and `spacing`/`fontSizes` (lines 170-175). A function-form `baseStyle` is resolved across **all 2^5 = 32** boolean prop combinations (`PROP_COMBINATIONS`, lines 236-243), because a value branch (`top: floated ? '3xs' : '50%'`) is invisible under the all-false default — the comment at lines 231-234 records that `'3xs'` shipped exactly that way. Results are deduplicated (lines 274-283).

1. **`collect() actually walks the registered recipes`** (line 287) — the **vacuity guard**. Asserts `Object.keys(components).length > 0` and `collect().length > 0`. Comment at lines 288-290: "Every other test here asserts an empty offender list, which an empty input satisfies just as well as a clean one. Without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green."
2. **`no sizing property uses a bare spacing-scale key`** (line 295) — `SIZING_PROPS` (width/height/min/max/boxSize/w/h/minW/maxW/minH/maxH, lines 118-132) × `SPACING_KEYS`. Catches `width: 'xl'` resolving to Chakra's `sizes.xl` = 36rem. This is the bug that shipped a 576px icon (header comment lines 9-13; the surviving countermeasure is visible at `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:12-16`).
3. **`no typography property uses a bare scale key`** (line 305) — `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` map (lines 153-157) covering `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing`, each against its own Zimmermann keys ∪ spacing keys. `fontWeight` is deliberately excluded because `medium` resolves to 500 in both scales (lines 149-151).
4. **`no compound shorthand contains a bare scale key`** (line 315) — for `padding`/`margin`/`inset`/`gap`/`p`/`m` only (`SPACE_SHORTHANDS`, line 160), splits the value on whitespace *outside* `var(...)` (line 321) and flags any part that is a spacing key. Catches `padding: 'xs 0'`, which the browser drops entirely.
5. **`no override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale`** (line 331) — the **house-style** guard, over `SPACE_PROPS` (44 entries, lines 70-113) and `COLOR_PROPS` (8 entries, line 116) against `SPACING_KEYS` and a recursively-flattened dotted `COLOR_KEYS` set (lines 60-66). Explicitly **not** a correctness bug (lines 28-34, 339-343): `space` and `colors` are registered, so the bare key resolves fine — it enforces `var(--zimm-*)` at every call site so reviewers don't have to consult the registered-scale list.
6. **`no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name`** (line 347) — since `extendTheme` deep-merges, a recipe named `Footer` would inherit SFCC's `Footer`. Compares each recipe's own `baseStyle` keys against the composed `theme.components[name]` keys; any key present after composition that wasn't declared came from the base. `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` (line 351) is the allow-list — everything else must be namespaced, which is why the recipes are `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmFooterNavColumn`, `ZimmFooterBottomBar` and not `Footer`.

**Self-declared blind spots**, written into the file header (lines 36-43): the walk sees the recipe map only, so it cannot catch the same mistakes as a JSX prop. Two live instances are named — `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` (`fontSize="l"`, emits nothing) and a former bare `paddingLeft: '2xs'` in `footerNavColumn/index.tsx`'s inline `sx` merge that "was only found by a manual grep".

**5.5 Other vacuity/anchoring guards.**
- `footer/index.stories.tsx:231-237` — anchors both operands of a before/after height comparison above zero, with the reasoning that `display:none`, `height:0`, and jsdom all measure 0 twice and would satisfy the equality vacuously.

- `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:41-46` — tests the *empty-and-focused* case specifically, because focus and filled resolve to the same colour in the light palette and only that case distinguishes "the focus branch ran" from "fell through to default".

## 7. ACCESSIBILITY

**7.1 Landmark and dialog semantics.** `<chakra.footer role="contentinfo">` (`footer/index.tsx:91`); `role="presentation"` backdrop + `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby aria-describedby` panel (`zimmModal/index.tsx:51-57`), with the ids supplied by the consumer and matched to real elements (`zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx:58-59,63,78`).

**7.2 Never render a false affordance.** A control that cannot act is a non-interactive element, not a disabled button — applied twice with the same reasoning (WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4): the locale placeholder renders as a `<div>` (`bottomBar/index.tsx:40-45`, and `bottomBar.css.ts:103-107` withholds `cursor`/`_focusVisible` to match), and an unusable contact channel renders as a labelled `<span>` (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:76-88`). The two comments cross-reference each other.

**7.3 Perceivable-but-inert.** The fallback span keeps the icon labelled rather than `aria-hidden`, so the channel is announced — the comment at `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:81-83` records that a previous `aria-hidden` caused WCAG 1.1.1 information loss.

**7.4 Icon aria is enforced at the type level.** `ZimmIconProps` is a discriminated XOR: `{'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never} | {'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string}` (`zimmIcon/index.tsx:93`), and `role="img"` is emitted only when a label is present (`zimmIcon/index.tsx:151`). Every decorative use passes `aria-hidden={true}` explicitly: `bottomBar/index.tsx:49`, `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:116`, `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:73`, `zimmButton/index.tsx:51`. **All sites.**

**7.5 Cross-origin links.** `target="_blank"` + explicit `rel="noopener noreferrer"` + a WCAG 3.2.5 accessible-name suffix, applied by scheme rather than by channel name (`zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:37,39-40,66-70`); `tel:`/`mailto:` deliberately get neither.

**7.6 Focus visibility.** `_focusVisible` with `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` (light) or a `--zimm-color-text-inverse` outline (dark), plus `outlineOffset`, in every interactive recipe: `zimmButton.css.ts:33-37,82-86,113-117,143-147,168-172,192-196`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts:58-62,66-70`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:156-162`, `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:27-31`, `footer.css.ts:135-139`. The footer wordmark button's reset exists specifically to restore the ring the anchor-less markup would lack (`footer.css.ts:126-128`). `zimmButton.css.ts:28-32` records that the previous `outline:none` + background swap was an actual WCAG 2.4.7 failure (`#191919` vs `#000000`).

**7.7 Target size (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, 24px).** `zimmTextInput.css.ts:151-154` (`minWidth`/`minHeight`), `zimmButton.css.ts:226-240` (`minW`/`minH` on the `icon` size — with the note that Chakra's `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0` as a style prop so any `p` here is silently discarded), `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:11,21-22`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts:20-23` (`minHeight` as a floor, not a fixed height, so wrapped labels grow).

**7.8 Form semantics.** `htmlFor`/`id` pairing via `useId` (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:69-71,93,97`), `aria-invalid`, computed `aria-describedby` joining helper+error ids (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:107-108`), `role="alert"` on the error paragraph (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:127`) and on the subscribe failure message (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:76`), `aria-live="polite"` on the subscribe state slot (`zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:62`), `autoComplete="email"` when `type==='email'` (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:103`).

**7.9 Dialog keyboard mechanics** live in `useZimmModal.ts`: focus save/restore around open/close (lines 48-63), body-scroll lock restoring the *previous* value (lines 66-73), Escape (line 78), and a Tab trap with a third branch for focus that has escaped the boundary entirely — WCAG 2.1.2, cited at lines 96-102.

**7.10 Semantic markup choices are argued in comments, not assumed.** `<ul>`/`<li>` for nav links with `display:flex` on the `<li>` and the 1.5px line-box measurement behind it (`footerNavColumn.css.ts:63-69`); the contact row placed as the *last child of the list* rather than a sibling (`footerNavColumn/index.tsx:84-88`); a `<button>` rather than `<a href>` for the wordmark to mirror the header (`footer/index.tsx:120-124`); `aria-label="Zimmermann home"` at line 125; `role="img"` + `aria-label` on the inline logo SVG (`zimmLogo/index.tsx:30-31`).

**7.11 Contrast is reasoned about in the recipe.** `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts:14-15` — `text.secondary` (#666, 5.74:1) chosen over `text.muted` (#969696), which "would fail WCAG AA 4.5:1 at 12px on the white modal panel". `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:55-58` — failure copy uses the coral inverse error colour so it doesn't read as success.

**7.12 Units are chosen for zoom (WCAG 1.4.4).** `footer.css.ts:6-9`, `zimmTextInput.css.ts:27-35` (a px `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT` broke a rem-derived slot at 200% zoom — reserved 90px against a 53px field), `zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts:10-11`.
